<doc title="Introduction" path="guide/index.md">
# Introduction

Simba is a JVM library for **leader election and distributed locks**. Each process opens one *session* on a backend
you already operate (MySQL or PostgreSQL, Redis, or Zookeeper) and contends for named *leases* on it. The node that
wins a lease gets a *term*: an object that carries a fencing token and knows how long it is still valid. There is no
Simba server: the library runs inside your application.

Typical uses: run a scheduled job on one node only, spread partitions of work over the live nodes, have one process
drive a workflow, or hold a lock around a step that must not run twice at once.

## What Simba Guarantees

1. **At most one valid term per lease name, as far as the local clock can tell.** A term is valid until the session's
   local deadline, which always comes before the backend could hand the lease to another session (as long as clock
   rates differ by less than the configured `drift`). Validity is computed from the monotonic clock on every read, so
   a process waking from a long pause sees its term as invalid on the first read.
2. **Fencing tokens.** Every term carries a token greater than zero that strictly increases from term to term of the
   same name, on every backend.
3. **Paired callbacks.** Every `onElected(term)` is followed by exactly one `onRevoked(term, reason)`, callbacks of one
   election run one at a time in order, and none arrives after `stop()` completed.
4. **Ordered handover.** `stop()` and `stepDown()` interrupt the work bound to the term, wait for it to exit (at most
   for the term's remaining time), and only then release the lease.
5. **Liveness.** A node that closes its client frees its leases at once; when a node crashes or loses the backend,
   its session expires after `leaseDuration` and the other nodes take its leases over.

## What Simba Does Not Guarantee

A term is a *weakly consistent view* of the backend. A process paused by GC, a stalled disk or a network partition can
resume after its session expired and still finish a write it already started, while another node holds a newer term.
No lease-based lock can prevent that on its own; Simba never promises "no split-brain".

If overlapping work is harmful, the protected resource must reject stale owners: send
[`term.token`](/guide/correctness#fencing-tokens) with every write and let the resource refuse tokens lower than the
highest it has accepted. If duplicated work is merely wasteful (a report generated twice), the term alone is enough.

Simba also does not keep working while the backend is unreachable: once the session's local deadline passes, every
term of that node is revoked.

## Choose an API

All APIs hang off one `Simba` client (one per process, one backend session).

| You want to... | Use | Page |
|---|---|---|
| React to gaining and losing leadership | `simba.election(name).start(listener)` | [Quick Start](/guide/quick-start#election) |
| Run a block once per term, interrupted when the term ends | `election.runWhileLeader { term -> }` | [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work#run-while-leader) |
| Run a method periodically on the leader only | `election.schedule(...)` or `@SimbaScheduled` | [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work#schedules) |
| Spread N partitions over the live nodes, each partition on one node | `simba.group(name, n)` or `@SimbaPartitioned` | [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work#partition-groups) |
| Hold a lock around a step, then release it | `simba.lock(name).acquire(timeout)` | [Locks](/guide/locks) |
| See the session and every election of this node | `simba.snapshot()`, Actuator `simba` | [Observability](/guide/observability) |

## Choose a Backend

| | JDBC (MySQL 8, PostgreSQL 14+) | Redis 7 | Zookeeper |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session | Row in `simba_session` | Hash `simba:session:{sid}` with `PX` | A Zookeeper session |
| Lease | Row in `simba_lease`, never deleted | Hash `simba:lease:{name}`, never expires | Ephemeral node `/simba/leases/{name}` |
| Fencing token | Counter in the row, `+1` per term | Counter in the hash, `+1` per term | The node's `czxid` |
| Clock | Database time | Redis `TIME` | Zookeeper session timeout |
| Failover after a clean stop | Next candidate attempt | Immediate (release broadcast) | Immediate (node watch) |
| Token durability | Transactional | Can go back after a failover | Zookeeper quorum |

Failover after a crash takes about `leaseDuration` (Zookeeper: the negotiated session timeout) plus the next
candidate attempt. Pick the one you already run; read
[Backends](/guide/backends) for the setup and operating notes, in particular the
[Redis failover boundary](/guide/backends#token-regression-after-a-failover).

## Where to Next

- [Quick Start](/guide/quick-start): add the dependency and run code.
- [Concepts and Correctness](/guide/correctness): sessions, leases, terms, tokens and the handover order. Read this
  before protecting anything that must not be written twice.
- [Spring Boot](/guide/configuration), [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work), [Locks](/guide/locks),
  [Observability](/guide/observability), [Testing](/guide/testing).
- Coming from Simba 4.x: [Migrating to 5.0](/guide/migration).
- [Architecture](/architecture/) and [Contributing](/contributing/) if you work on Simba itself.
</doc>

<doc title="Quick Start" path="guide/quick-start.md">
# Quick Start

Simba 5 needs Java 21 or later (work and backend calls run on virtual threads). The starter needs Spring Boot 4
(4.1 or later); the libraries are compiled for Kotlin 2.2 or later.

## Dependencies

Add the Spring Boot starter and **one** backend module.

::: code-group

```kotlin [Gradle (Kotlin)]
implementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-spring-boot-starter:${simbaVersion}")

// JDBC: MySQL 8 or PostgreSQL 14+
implementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-jdbc:${simbaVersion}")
implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-jdbc")
runtimeOnly("com.mysql:mysql-connector-j") // or org.postgresql:postgresql

// or Redis 7 (through Spring Data Redis)
implementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-spring-redis:${simbaVersion}")
implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-redis")

// or Zookeeper
implementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-zookeeper:${simbaVersion}")

// optional, since 5.1: suspending lock calls, withLock, event Flow
implementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-coroutines:${simbaVersion}")
```

```xml [Maven]
<dependency>
    <groupId>me.ahoo.simba</groupId>
    <artifactId>simba-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
    <version>${simba.version}</version>
</dependency>
<!-- plus one of: simba-jdbc, simba-spring-redis, simba-zookeeper -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>me.ahoo.simba</groupId>
    <artifactId>simba-spring-redis</artifactId>
    <version>${simba.version}</version>
</dependency>
<!-- optional, since 5.1: coroutine adapters -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>me.ahoo.simba</groupId>
    <artifactId>simba-coroutines</artifactId>
    <version>${simba.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

:::

`simba-bom` aligns the versions of every Simba module. `simba-coroutines` (since 5.1) adds suspending lock calls, `withLock` and a `Flow` of events on top of any backend; see [Locks](/guide/locks#coroutines). Without Spring, depend on `simba-core` plus a backend module:
`simba-jdbc`, `simba-zookeeper`, or for Redis `simba-spring-redis` (which brings `simba-redis`). `simba-redis` alone
only defines the `RedisScripting` port: use it without `simba-spring-redis` only with your own adapter for another
Redis client.

## Backend Setup

| Backend | What you provide | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| JDBC | One `DataSource` bean and the three tables | Run [`init-simba-mysql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-mysql.sql) or [`init-simba-postgresql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-postgresql.sql) once; the dialect is detected from the `DataSource` |
| Redis | One `RedisConnectionFactory` bean (Spring Boot creates it from `spring.data.redis.*`) | Redis 7; standalone, Sentinel or Cluster |
| Zookeeper | `simba.zookeeper.connect-string` | Simba opens its own Zookeeper clients, one per session |

The scripts are on the classpath of `simba-jdbc`, so Spring Boot can run them for you:

```yaml
spring:
  sql:
    init:
      mode: always
      schema-locations: classpath:me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-mysql.sql
```

With more than one backend module on the classpath, set `simba.backend=jdbc|redis|zookeeper`; startup fails
otherwise. The [Backends](/guide/backends) page has the schema, the keys and the operating notes of each.

The starter creates one `Simba` bean. Inject it wherever you need an API below.

## Election

The base API: callbacks when this node gains and loses a term.

```kotlin
val election = simba.election("order-dispatcher")
election.start(object : LeadershipListener {
    override fun onElected(term: Term) = dispatcher.start(term.token)
    override fun onRevoked(term: Term, reason: RevokeReason) = dispatcher.stop()
})

// on shutdown: completes after the last onRevoked ran
election.stop().toCompletableFuture().join()
```

Every `onElected(term)` is followed by exactly one `onRevoked(term, reason)`. Keep callbacks short; they run one at a
time per election.

## Leader Work

Usually you want code to run *while* this node leads. `runWhileLeader` runs a block once per term, on its own virtual
thread, and interrupts it when the term ends:

```kotlin
val task = simba.election("report").runWhileLeader { term ->
    while (term.isValid) {
        reportStore.writeChunk(nextChunk(), fencingToken = term.token)
    }
}
// later
task.close()
```

Periodic work on the leader only:

::: code-group

```kotlin [Kotlin]
simba.election("report").schedule(Schedule.fixedDelay(Duration.ofMinutes(1))) { term ->
    reportService.generate(fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

```java [Spring]
@Service
public class ReportJobs {
    @SimbaScheduled(name = "report", fixedDelay = "1m")
    public void generate(Term term) {
        reportService.generate(term.getToken());
    }
}
```

:::

See [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work) for schedules, handover and partition groups.

## Lock

`acquire` returns a `LockTerm`: the credential of the lock. Closing it releases the lease.

```kotlin
simba.lock("invoice-42").acquire(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).use { term ->
    term.ensureValid(Duration.ofSeconds(2))      // enough time left for this step?
    invoiceStore.write(invoice, fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

`acquire` throws `LockTimeoutException` when no term was won in time; `tryAcquire()` makes one attempt and returns
`null` instead. See [Locks](/guide/locks).

## Partition Group

Spread partitions over the live nodes; each partition runs on exactly one node at a time.

::: code-group

```kotlin [Kotlin]
simba.group("billing", partitions = 16).schedule(Schedule.fixedDelay(Duration.ofMinutes(1))) { term, partition ->
    billing.run(shard = partition, fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

```java [Spring]
@SimbaPartitioned(group = "billing", partitions = 16, fixedDelay = "1m")
public void bill(Term term, int partition) {
    billing.run(partition, term.getToken());
}
```

:::

## Without Spring

Build the client yourself over a backend; `Simba` is `AutoCloseable` and closing it frees every lease at once.

```kotlin
val backend = JdbcLeaseBackend.postgres(dataSource)          // or JdbcLeaseBackend.mysql(dataSource)
// val backend = RedisLeaseBackend(SpringRedisScripting(redisConnectionFactory))
// val backend = ZookeeperLeaseBackend("zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181")

Simba.builder()
    .backend(backend)
    .config(SimbaConfig.builder().leaseDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(15)).build())
    .listener { event -> log.debug { "simba: $event" } }
    .build()
    .use { simba ->
        simba.election("report").schedule(Schedule.fixedRate(Duration.ofMinutes(1))) { term -> report(term.token) }
        awaitShutdown()
    }
backend.close()
```

Create one `Simba` per process: every election, lock and group shares its session, so one keep-alive renews all of
them. The [Spring Boot](/guide/configuration#without-spring) page lists the builder options.

## Run the Example

The [example application](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/tree/main/simba-example) uses `@SimbaScheduled`,
`@SimbaPartitioned` and an election against the backend you choose:

```bash
./gradlew simba-example:run -PexampleBackend=redis   # jdbc | redis | zookeeper
```

Start it twice and stop one instance to watch the other take over.
</doc>

<doc title="Concepts and Correctness" path="guide/correctness.md">
# Concepts and Correctness

A distributed lock cannot know that its holder is still alive; it can only *lease* ownership for a bounded time.
Everything Simba guarantees follows from that. This page explains the model, the timing, and what your code has to do
when overlapping work must never happen. The design is recorded in
[ADR 0010](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-simba-5-target-architecture.md).

## The Model in One Picture

```mermaid
graph LR
    P["Simba client<br>(one per process)"] -->|"opens, keeps alive"| S["Session<br>SessionId, expires on the backend"]
    S -->|"owns"| L1["Lease 'report'<br>token 7"]
    S -->|"owns"| L2["Lease 'billing.3'<br>token 12"]
    L1 -.->|"seen locally as"| T1["Term<br>name, token, isValid, remaining()"]
    L2 -.->|"seen locally as"| T2["Term"]
    style P fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style S fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style L1 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style L2 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style T1 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style T2 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

## Sessions

Liveness belongs to the node, not to each lock. A `Simba` client opens **one session** on the backend and renews it
with one keep-alive every `renewInterval`; every lease the node holds and every group it joined lives and dies with
that session. Renewal cost is one call per node, whatever the number of leases.

- A `SessionId` identifies one session *incarnation* and is never reused: random 128 bits on JDBC and Redis, the
  Zookeeper session id on Zookeeper.
- An expired session is **never revived**. The backend answers `Expired` to its keep-alive and refuses its acquires;
  the client opens a new session (a new id) and contends again. Otherwise a lease another node had taken over in the
  meantime could become "mine" again.
- `close()` closes the session, so the backend frees every lease of the node at once.

The session status, visible in [`snapshot()`](/guide/observability#snapshot), is `OPENING` (no session yet, or a new
one after the last expired), `LIVE` (last keep-alive succeeded), `SUSPENDED` (last keep-alive failed, deadline not
passed) or `CLOSED`.

## The Local Deadline

The client never compares wall clocks with the backend. Each keep-alive reply carries the session's remaining time as
a *duration* measured by the backend, and the client turns it into a deadline on its own monotonic clock:

```
deadline = sentAt + remaining × (1 − drift) − margin
```

`sentAt` is when the keep-alive was **sent**, not when the reply arrived, so a slow reply only shortens the deadline.
Every backend call times out after the renew period in effect (shorter when the backend grants less than the lease),
so a stuck call never holds the only keep-alive slot past the retries left before the deadline. As long as the two
clocks run at rates within `1 ± drift` of each other, the local deadline passes before the backend
can expire the session and give its leases to someone else. Once the local deadline has passed, a renewal that arrives
late never extends it: the session ends (`DEADLINE_PASSED`) and its terms stay ended.

## Leases, Terms and Tokens

A **lease** is a backend record `name → (session, token)`. Lease names are 1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`,
other than `.` and `..`, on every backend, so a name means the same as a Redis key, a Zookeeper path and a JDBC column.

A **term** is one period during which this node owns a lease. Winning the same name twice gives two different
`Term` objects. A term carries:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The lease name |
| `token` | Fencing token: greater than zero, constant within the term, strictly increasing across terms of the name |
| `isValid` | Not revoked and the session's local deadline has not passed |
| `remaining()` | Time left before the local deadline; `Duration.ZERO` once the term ended |
| `ensureValid(minRemaining)` | Throws `TermExpiredException` unless the term is valid for more than `minRemaining` |
| `revoked` | `CompletionStage<RevokeReason>` that completes exactly once, when the term ends |

`isValid` and `remaining()` are pure functions of the monotonic clock and the session's deadline: no watchdog thread
has to run first, so a process that wakes from a long pause sees `false` on its first read, and an ended term never
becomes valid again even if the node is re-elected.

A term ends for one of these reasons:

| `RevokeReason` | When |
|---|---|
| `STOPPED` | The election was stopped, the lock released, or the client closed |
| `STEPPED_DOWN` | The election stepped down |
| `DEADLINE_PASSED` | The session's local deadline passed without a successful keep-alive |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED` | The backend reported the session expired |
| `TAKEN_OVER` | A keep-alive reply no longer lists the lease as owned by this session |

A term is always revoked **before** its lease is released, and every release carries the term's token, so a release
that arrives late cannot free a later term.

## Timing

| `SimbaConfig` | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `leaseDuration` | 15 s | The backend expires a session this long after its last keep-alive |
| `renewInterval` | `leaseDuration / 3` | Keep-alive period |
| `drift` | 0.01 | Upper bound of the clock rate difference between a node and the backend, in `[0, 0.5)` |
| `margin` | 50 ms | Extra safety subtracted from every deadline |
| `retryJitter` | `renewInterval / 2` | Candidates retry after `renewInterval / 2` plus a random delay in `[0, retryJitter)` |
| `minBackoff` | 100 ms | Lower bound of the backoff after a failed keep-alive |

Build it with `SimbaConfig.builder()` (`toBuilder()` derives a variant); `build()` fails unless
`renewInterval × 2 ≤ leaseDuration` (at least two keep-alive attempts fit before the deadline) and
`leaseDuration × (1 − drift) − margin > renewInterval` (otherwise every term would flap). In Spring Boot these are the
[`simba.session.*`](/guide/configuration#properties) properties.

A backend may grant less than `leaseDuration` — a Zookeeper server caps the session timeout at its
`maxSessionTimeout`. When two keep-alives at `renewInterval` no longer fit in the local validity it grants, the client
renews every third of that validity instead and publishes `SessionLeaseShortened` (and a warning) once per session,
rather than letting every term end with `DEADLINE_PASSED`.

How to choose:

- **`leaseDuration`** bounds failover after a crash or a partition: the other nodes can take a lease over only after
  the session expired on the backend. Shorter means faster failover but less tolerance for slow backend calls and GC
  pauses.
- **`renewInterval`** is how often the node calls the backend. A keep-alive call times out after one renew interval;
  after a failure the client retries with halving backoff (half the time left, capped at `renewInterval`, at least
  `minBackoff`) until the deadline.
- **`drift`** and **`margin`** only shorten the local view of the lease; raise them if your hosts' clocks are poorly
  disciplined or run in VMs that can be paused.

## Candidates

A node that wants a lease and does not hold it is a *candidate*. Candidates attempt to acquire every
`renewInterval / 2` plus jitter. Redis and Zookeeper also broadcast releases, so a clean stop of the leader is taken
over at once there; on JDBC the next attempt picks it up. At most one acquire per election is in flight.

A term is adopted only from the reply to the election's current attempt, received before the session's local
deadline, and only with a token above every token this session released for the name. A late reply to an abandoned
attempt releases what it won.

## Fencing Tokens

A term's validity is a hint for when to *start* a step, never proof that nobody else owns the lease. Only the
protected resource can reject a stale owner, and it needs the token to do so:

1. Pass `term.token` with every write to the protected resource.
2. The resource accepts the write only if the token is **at least** the highest token it has accepted, and records
   it. Equal tokens must be accepted: retries within one term carry the same token.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
autonumber
    participant A as Node A (token 7)
    participant B as Node B (token 8)
    participant R as Resource
    A->>A: paused by GC, session expires
    B->>R: write(token 8) accepted, highest = 8
    A->>R: write(token 7) after waking up
    R-->>A: rejected (7 < 8)
```

### Checking Tokens in the Resource

The check and the write must be **one atomic step**. Reading the highest token first and writing afterwards lets a
stale owner pass the check and land its write after a newer owner.

**SQL** — one conditional `UPDATE`; zero matched rows means a stale owner:

```sql
-- once per resource: insert ignore into ledger_state (id) values (?);
update ledger_state
set last_batch = ?, fencing_token = ?
where id = ? and fencing_token <= ?;
```

MySQL Connector/J reports matched rows by default, so a retry with the same token and values still counts as `1`.

**Redis** — one Lua script; keep the token and the value in the same hash slot (`{resource}`) for Redis Cluster:

```lua
-- KEYS[1] = {resource}:token, KEYS[2] = {resource}:value, ARGV[1] = token, ARGV[2] = value
local highest = tonumber(redis.call('get', KEYS[1]) or '0')
if tonumber(ARGV[1]) < highest then
    return 0
end
redis.call('set', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
redis.call('set', KEYS[2], ARGV[2])
return 1
```

**In one JVM** — check and write under the same lock:

```kotlin
synchronized(state) {
    if (fencingToken < state.highestToken) return false
    state.highestToken = fencingToken
    state.write(value)
    return true
}
```

### Verifying a Resource

`simba-tck` ships `FencingSpec`, a JUnit test kit for your own resource; see
[Testing](/guide/testing#verifying-a-fencing-resource). The recipes above pass it
([`JdbcFencingRecipeTest`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/test/kotlin/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/JdbcFencingRecipeTest.kt),
[`RedisFencingRecipeTest`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-redis/src/test/kotlin/me/ahoo/simba/redis/RedisFencingRecipeTest.kt)).

| Backend | Token source | Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| JDBC | `simba_lease.token`, `+1` per term | Rows are never deleted, so the token never resets |
| Redis | `token` field of `simba:lease:{name}`, `+1` per term | Asynchronous replication: [can go back after a failover](/guide/backends#token-regression-after-a-failover) |
| Zookeeper | `czxid` of the lease node | Strictly increasing but not consecutive |

## Checking the Term Before Each Step

`term.ensureValid(minRemaining)` throws `TermExpiredException` unless the term stays valid for more than
`minRemaining`. Call it before a step that should not start when the term is about to end:

```kotlin
simba.election("ledger").runWhileLeader { term ->
    for (batch in batches) {
        term.ensureValid(Duration.ofSeconds(2))   // expected duration of one batch
        ledger.settle(batch, fencingToken = term.token)
    }
}
```

This narrows the window in which an expired owner starts new work; it does not close it. A pause *after* the check is
still possible, which is why the resource must check the token.

## Handover Order

`stop()` and `stepDown(cooldown)` give the lease up in a fixed order when the election runs work
(`runWhileLeader`, `schedule`, a partition group, `@SimbaScheduled`, `@SimbaPartitioned`):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
autonumber
    participant U as Caller
    participant E as Engine
    participant W as Leader work
    participant B as Backend
    U->>E: stop() / stepDown(cooldown)
    E->>W: revoke term (isValid = false), interrupt
    W-->>E: work exits (or the term's local deadline passes)
    E->>B: release(name, token)
    E->>U: onRevoked(term, STOPPED / STEPPED_DOWN), future completes
```

The lease stays held until the work exited or the session's local deadline at the stop passed, whichever comes first,
so no other node starts the same work while the old run is still finishing. Work that ignores interruption therefore
delays the handover up to the term's remaining time. Terms without work release at once.

A term lost any other way (deadline, take-over, session expiry) is not waited for: the backend may already have given
the lease to another node, so the work is interrupted and the term revoked immediately.

`stepDown(cooldown)` keeps the election started but does not contend for `cooldown`, counted from the step-down: use
it to move leadership off a node before a deploy or to drain it. `stop()` ends the election.

## Callbacks and Lifecycle

- Every `onElected(term)` is followed by exactly one `onRevoked(term, reason)` for the same term.
- Callbacks of one election run one at a time, in order, on a serial dispatcher over the callback executor (virtual
  threads by default). No internal lock is held while they run, and the engine never waits for a callback except
  through the futures of `stop()` and `stepDown()`.
- `stop()` and `stepDown()` return a `CompletionStage<Void>` that completes after the last `onRevoked` ran; after
  `stop()` completes, the listener receives nothing more.
- `start(listener)` throws `IllegalStateException` while the same name is already started on this client.
- Blocking `close()` methods (`Simba`, `LeaderTask`, `LockTerm`, `GroupTask`) do not wait when called from a
  callback or from leader work, where waiting would wait for itself.
- With a direct callback executor, callbacks run on the engine loop: chain on the stages the client returns there.
  Converting a pending one with `toCompletableFuture()` throws `IllegalStateException`, since waiting for it would
  block the loop that completes it.
- If the callback executor rejects an `onElected`, nobody learns of the term and its work never starts: the election
  steps down for one lease duration, and that term's `onRevoked` is not delivered either, so callbacks stay paired.

## Failure Modes

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Leader process crashes | Its session expires after `leaseDuration` (Zookeeper: the session timeout); a candidate acquires at its next attempt. |
| Leader stops cleanly | Work exits, the lease is released; Redis and Zookeeper candidates acquire at once, JDBC candidates at their next attempt. |
| Backend unreachable | Session `SUSPENDED`, keep-alive retried with backoff; at the local deadline every term of the node is revoked (`DEADLINE_PASSED`) and a new session is opened once the backend answers. Nothing keeps running as leader meanwhile. |
| Backend reports the session expired | Every term revoked (`SESSION_EXPIRED`), new session, contend again. |
| Leader paused longer than the lease (GC, VM freeze) | On waking, `term.isValid` is already `false`; the engine revokes the term. Writes already in flight can still land: the [fencing token](#fencing-tokens) is the only defense. |
| Keep-alive shows the lease owned by someone else | Term revoked (`TAKEN_OVER`). |
| Clock rate differs by more than `drift` | The safety argument no longer holds; raise `drift`. |
| Redis failover loses recent writes | A token can go back; see [Backends](/guide/backends#token-regression-after-a-failover). |
| Failover to an asynchronous database replica (MySQL replica, PostgreSQL standby promotion) | Like a Redis failover: recent token increments and keep-alives can be lost, so a token can go back. Use synchronous replication when fencing must hold; see [Backends](/guide/backends#operating-notes). |
| Backend host's clock steps (NTP step, VM migration) | JDBC and Redis measure leases with that clock, so every lease shortens (forward step) or lengthens (backward step) at once. A forward step can expire a holder's lease on the backend while its local deadline has not passed: another node can win a term while the old holder still reads `isValid`. This is not rate drift and `drift` does not cover it; only the fencing token protects. Run the backend hosts with slewing time sync. |
</doc>

<doc title="Backends" path="guide/backends.md">
# Backends

Every backend implements the same `LeaseBackend` SPI and passes the same
[TCK](/guide/testing#backend-tck), so elections, locks and groups behave the same on all of them. They differ in
storage, in where time is measured, and in how durable the fencing token is.

Every backend follows the same rules: a session expires once it was not kept alive for its lease; an expired session
is never revived; a lease belongs to a session only while that session is live; a lease's token is greater than zero,
strictly increases with every new term and never resets; and every remaining time is measured by the backend's clock
and returned as a duration.

## JDBC (MySQL 8, PostgreSQL 14+)

Module `simba-jdbc`, class `JdbcLeaseBackend` with a `Dialect` (`Dialect.MYSQL`, `Dialect.POSTGRESQL`):

```kotlin
val backend = JdbcLeaseBackend.mysql(dataSource)      // or JdbcLeaseBackend.postgres(dataSource)
```

### Schema

Create the three tables once with the script of your database:
[`init-simba-mysql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-mysql.sql)
or
[`init-simba-postgresql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-postgresql.sql)
(both on the classpath under `me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/`). The MySQL version:

```sql
create table if not exists simba_session
(
    session_id char(32) character set ascii collate ascii_bin not null primary key,
    expires_at bigint                                        not null comment 'database time, epoch ms',
    metadata   varchar(1024)                                 not null default '',
    index idx_session_expires (expires_at)
);

create table if not exists simba_lease
(
    name       varchar(128) character set ascii collate ascii_bin not null primary key,
    session_id char(32) character set ascii collate ascii_bin     not null default '' comment 'empty = free',
    token      bigint                                             not null comment 'term number, never reset',
    index idx_lease_session (session_id)
);

create table if not exists simba_member
(
    group_name varchar(128) character set utf8mb4 collate utf8mb4_bin not null,
    session_id char(32) character set ascii collate ascii_bin not null,
    primary key (group_name, session_id),
    index idx_member_session (session_id)
);
```

| Table | One row per | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `simba_session` | Session | `expires_at` in database time; one `UPDATE` per keep-alive renews the session and, through it, every lease and membership of the node |
| `simba_lease` | Lease name ever acquired | Never deleted, so the token never resets; release sets `session_id` to `''` and keeps the token |
| `simba_member` | Group member | Live only while its session is |

Lease and group names are case-sensitive (binary collations on MySQL, `"C"` on PostgreSQL).

### How It Works

- A lease belongs to the session in `session_id` only while that session's `expires_at` is in the future. Acquire is
  one upsert that takes the row when it is free or its session expired and advances `token` by one. On MySQL the
  `token` assignment comes first in `SET`, because MySQL evaluates `SET` left to right with already-updated values.
- The take-over reads the holder's session row with a shared lock (`for share`), so it serializes with that session's
  keep-alive at any isolation level: a renewal that commits concurrently either wins, or sees the lease gone in the
  same keep-alive reply.
- Every time comparison uses the database's own clock (`now`: UTC epoch milliseconds, constant within a statement and
  independent of the connection's time zone), so application hosts' clocks never matter.
- Expired sessions are cleaned up lazily: a lease of an expired session is free for the next acquirer, and a
  keep-alive that finds its session expired removes it. The rest (sessions of crashed processes) is removed by
  `purgeExpired()`, which runs at most once per `purgeInterval` (default one minute) after an `openSession` or
  `keepAlive`, up to 1000 sessions per run, along `idx_session_expires`.

### Operating Notes

- A release does not notify anyone: after a clean stop, candidates take over at their next attempt
  (`renewInterval / 2` plus jitter).
- Each statement has a timeout; the starter sets it to the session renew interval (`simba.jdbc.query-timeout`), after
  which the engine gives up on the call anyway. Without Spring, `JdbcLeaseBackend` defaults to 5 s
  (`DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, the default renew interval); pass your renew interval as `queryTimeout` when you change it.
- Give Simba a connection pool that is not starved by the application: a keep-alive that waits for a connection
  longer than the renew interval counts as failed.
- Tokens and session expiries are only as durable as the database's commits. A failover to an asynchronous MySQL
  replica, or the promotion of a PostgreSQL standby that had not received the latest WAL, can lose recent token
  increments and keep-alives, exactly like a [Redis failover](#token-regression-after-a-failover): a token can go back.
  Keep fencing strict across failovers with synchronous replication (MySQL semi-synchronous replication or Group
  Replication, PostgreSQL `synchronous_commit` with synchronous standbys).
- Leases are measured with the database server's wall clock. A step of that clock (an NTP step, a VM migration)
  shortens or lengthens every lease at once, which is not the rate drift that `simba.session.drift` covers; see
  [Failure Modes](/guide/correctness#failure-modes).

## Redis 7

Module `simba-redis` (driver-neutral, Lua scripts behind the `RedisScripting` port) and `simba-spring-redis`
(`SpringRedisScripting`, the Spring Data Redis adapter). `SpringRedisScripting` needs Lettuce, the Spring Boot default
client: with Jedis, subscriptions block the calling thread and `WAIT` is unavailable, so the starter fails startup on a
non-Lettuce `RedisConnectionFactory`:

```kotlin
val backend = RedisLeaseBackend(SpringRedisScripting(redisConnectionFactory))
```

### Keys

| Key | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `simba:lease:{name}` | Hash, never expires | `session`, `token`, `expires` (Redis `TIME`); release clears `session` only, so the token never resets |
| `simba:session:{sid}` | Hash with `PX` = lease | The session; keep-alive, acquire and join fail once it is gone |
| `simba:session:{sid}:leases` | Set, same slot | Leases of the session |
| `simba:session:{sid}:groups` | Set, same slot | Groups the session joined |
| `simba:group:{group}` | Sorted set | Members (session ids) scored by expiry in Redis time |

Release publishes `released` on the lease key's channel (`simba:lease:{name}`); it is the only broadcast and lets
candidates take over at once. Every time decision uses Redis `TIME` inside the scripts.

Leases expire on their own: a new term lasts as long as its session (one full session lease on a Cluster), and a
keep-alive extends every lease the session holds, found through its lease index, so a lease acquired while a
keep-alive was in flight is extended too. Closing a session deletes it first, then frees its leases and memberships,
then drops its indexes, so a close repeated after a failure finishes the job.

### Cluster

On a Redis Cluster (`RedisScripting.clustered`, or `simba.redis.route-by-slot=true`) every script call keeps to one
hash slot: a call first touches the session's slot, then runs one script per slot of the remaining keys. Those later
scripts can reach Redis long after the first one (a starved thread, a driver holding commands until it reconnects),
when the session may have died. Each carries the session call's Redis time plus the session lease plus
`maxClockSkew` (constructor parameter, default 1 s): nothing is granted or extended beyond that point, and an acquire
or join that arrives after it changes nothing and fails. Keep-alive drops a lost lease from the session's index only
once no such acquire can still take it, so `owned` stays complete. The lease and session slots may live on nodes
whose clocks differ; a skew beyond `maxClockSkew` can end a lease before its session.

### Token Regression after a Failover

Redis replication is asynchronous. When a master fails before a replica received the latest `token` increment, the
promoted replica can hand out a token that was already used, or a lower one. A resource that checks tokens can then
accept a write from a node whose term is newer in time but lower in token, or reject a legitimate owner.

- Set `simba.redis.wait-replicas` (constructor parameter `waitReplicas`): a new term counts only once that many
  replicas acknowledged it with `WAIT`, otherwise the acquisition fails. This narrows the window; it does not close it,
  and it is not available on a Cluster.
- Enable persistence (AOF) so a restart of a single node does not reset tokens.
- When fencing must hold across failovers, use JDBC on synchronous replication or Zookeeper (quorum commits).
- Leases are measured with Redis `TIME`: a step of the Redis hosts' clocks shortens or lengthens every lease at once.

## Zookeeper

Module `simba-zookeeper`, class `ZookeeperLeaseBackend`:

```kotlin
val backend = ZookeeperLeaseBackend("zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181", root = "/simba")
```

### Nodes

| Path | Kind | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `{root}/leases/{name}` | Ephemeral | The session id; the owner is the node's `ephemeralOwner`, the token its `czxid` |
| `{root}/groups/{group}/{sessionId}` | Ephemeral, under a container node | Group member |

`root` defaults to `/simba`.

### How It Works

- A Simba session is one Zookeeper session: the backend opens a dedicated Zookeeper client per session (it does not
  use a shared Curator client) and never reconnects it to another session. The `SessionId` is the Zookeeper session id
  as 16 hex digits.
- The token is the lease node's `czxid`: strictly increasing across terms because zxids are global, but not
  consecutive.
- Release deletes the node; candidates watch it and take over at once. Group membership changes are watched too,
  including the creation of a group that did not exist yet.
- A name counts as possibly owned from the moment its create is sent, so a lease whose create succeeded but whose reply
  was lost (connection loss, timeout) is still reported by the next keep-alive, after checking the node's owner, and
  released by the engine. Releases of one session run one at a time.
- The Zookeeper client heartbeats on its own, so a local watchdog closes a session that no keep-alive renewed within
  the lease: a node that stopped renewing never keeps its leases through heartbeats alone.
- Remaining time is `min(leaseDuration, negotiated session timeout)`. While the client is disconnected, keep-alive and
  acquire fail, so the local deadline runs out; when Zookeeper reports the session expired, the session is `Expired`.

### Operating Notes

- The session timeout requested is `leaseDuration`; the ensemble clamps it to `[minSessionTimeout,
  maxSessionTimeout]` (by default 2 to 20 ticks). Failover after a crash takes the negotiated timeout.
- `simba.zookeeper.connection-timeout` bounds how long opening a session may take.
- Writes commit through a quorum, so a leader change keeps every token; tokens can only go back if the ensemble's data
  is lost or restored from an older snapshot. Session timeouts are tracked with the servers' elapsed time, so a wall
  clock step on an ensemble host does not shorten them.
- Group names follow the `LeaseName` rules (1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, not `.` or `..`), as on every
  backend. `members` syncs the group path first, so a join that just returned is always in the view.

### Security

By default the nodes get `OPEN_ACL_UNSAFE`: any client of the ensemble can delete or pre-create lease nodes and forge
group members. On a shared ensemble, authenticate and restrict the ACL:

```kotlin
val backend = ZookeeperLeaseBackend(
    "zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181",
    authInfo = listOf(AuthInfo("digest", "simba:secret".toByteArray())),
    aclProvider = myAclProvider, // e.g. ZooDefs.Ids.CREATOR_ALL_ACL for every path
    clientConfig = ZKClientConfig(), // TLS or SASL settings, optional
)
```

- Every client (each session's and the one `members` reads with) adds `authInfo` and is built with `clientConfig`.
- Every node the backend creates gets the ACL of `aclProvider`, including the parents it creates. Parents that already
  exist keep their ACL, and the ACL of `{root}/leases` and `{root}/groups/{group}` decides who may create or delete
  leases and members: create them with the backend's identity, or set their ACL yourself.
- Spring Boot: `simba.zookeeper.auth.scheme` / `simba.zookeeper.auth.credentials` and `simba.zookeeper.acl`
  (`auto` gives creator-only nodes once credentials are set); an `ACLProvider` bean replaces the ACL and a
  `ZKClientConfig` bean configures every client (see [Configuration](./configuration.md)).

## Selecting a Backend in Spring Boot

Each backend auto-configuration activates when its module is on the classpath, `simba.enabled` and
`simba.<backend>.enabled` are not `false`, and `simba.backend` is unset or names it. It defines the `LeaseBackend`
bean unless the application defines one.

With several backend modules on the classpath, set `simba.backend=jdbc|redis|zookeeper`; startup fails otherwise, and
also when `simba.backend` names a backend that is not active. To use a backend the starter does not configure (or a
`LeaseBackend` of your own), define the `LeaseBackend` bean yourself. See [Spring Boot](/guide/configuration).
</doc>

<doc title="Spring Boot" path="guide/configuration.md">
# Spring Boot

`simba-spring-boot-starter` builds one `Simba` client over the backend on the classpath, runs `@SimbaScheduled` and
`@SimbaPartitioned` methods, and adds Micrometer metrics, the `simba` Actuator endpoint and the `simba` health
indicator.

## Properties

| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `simba.enabled` | `true` | Enables the whole auto-configuration |
| `simba.backend` | — | `jdbc`, `redis` or `zookeeper`; required when several backend modules are active |
| `simba.session.lease-duration` | `15s` | The backend expires the session this long after its last keep-alive |
| `simba.session.renew-interval` | `lease-duration / 3` | Keep-alive period; at most half of the lease duration |
| `simba.session.drift` | `0.01` | Upper bound of the clock rate difference between a node and the backend, in `[0, 0.5)` |
| `simba.session.margin` | `50ms` | Extra safety subtracted from every local deadline |
| `simba.jdbc.enabled` | `true` | Enables the JDBC backend |
| `simba.jdbc.dialect` | detected | `mysql` or `postgresql`; detected from the `DataSource` when unset |
| `simba.jdbc.query-timeout` | renew interval | Per-statement timeout |
| `simba.redis.enabled` | `true` | Enables the Redis backend |
| `simba.redis.wait-replicas` | `0` | When positive, a new term counts only once that many replicas acknowledged it (`WAIT`); not on a Cluster |
| `simba.redis.wait-timeout` | `1s` | How long `WAIT` waits |
| `simba.redis.route-by-slot` | `true` on a Cluster | Split script calls by hash slot |
| `simba.zookeeper.enabled` | `true` | Enables the Zookeeper backend |
| `simba.zookeeper.connect-string` | `localhost:2181` | Ensemble the backend opens its sessions on |
| `simba.zookeeper.root` | `/simba` | Parent path of the lease and group nodes |
| `simba.zookeeper.connection-timeout` | `15s` | How long opening a session may take |
| `simba.zookeeper.auth.scheme` | `digest` | Authentication scheme every Zookeeper client adds |
| `simba.zookeeper.auth.credentials` | — | Auth data of the scheme (UTF-8), e.g. `user:password` for `digest`; unset: no authentication |
| `simba.zookeeper.acl` | `auto` | ACL of the nodes the backend creates: `open` (`OPEN_ACL_UNSAFE`), `creator` (`CREATOR_ALL_ACL`, needs credentials) or `auto` (`creator` with credentials, else `open`); an `ACLProvider` bean takes precedence |
| `simba.scheduling.enabled` | `true` | Runs `@SimbaScheduled` and `@SimbaPartitioned` methods |
| `simba.metrics.enabled` | `true` | Records Micrometer metrics when a `MeterRegistry` bean exists |
| `management.health.simba.enabled` | `true` | The `simba` health indicator |

The session properties are explained in [Concepts and Correctness](/guide/correctness#timing); invalid combinations
fail startup. A typical configuration:

```yaml
simba:
  backend: redis            # only needed with several backend modules on the classpath
  session:
    lease-duration: 15s
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,simba
```

## Beans the Starter Creates

| Bean | Condition |
|---|---|
| `LeaseBackend` (`JdbcLeaseBackend`, `RedisLeaseBackend` or `ZookeeperLeaseBackend`) | The backend is active and the application defines no `LeaseBackend`; JDBC needs a single `DataSource`, Redis a single `RedisConnectionFactory`; Zookeeper uses an `ACLProvider` and a `ZKClientConfig` bean when present |
| `Simba` | A `LeaseBackend` bean exists; built with `simba.session.*` and every `SimbaEventListener` bean |
| `SimbaLifecycle` | Closes the client on shutdown |
| `SimbaScheduledBeanPostProcessor` | `simba.scheduling.enabled` |
| `MicrometerSimbaEventListener` | Micrometer on the classpath, a `MeterRegistry` bean, `simba.metrics.enabled` |
| `SimbaEndpoint` (`simba`) | Actuator on the classpath and the endpoint available (enabled and exposed) |
| `SimbaHealthIndicator` (`simba`) | Actuator on the classpath and `management.health.simba.enabled` |

Every bean except the infrastructure (`SimbaBackendSelection`, the startup check of `simba.backend`, and
`SimbaScheduledBeanPostProcessor`) is `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`: define your own to replace it. To customize the
client beyond the properties (executors, a fixed seed), define the `Simba` bean yourself with `Simba.builder()`.

## Annotated Methods

`@SimbaScheduled` runs a bean method on the leader of an election; `@SimbaPartitioned` runs it for every partition of
a group this node leads. Both start after the context refreshed and stop on shutdown. Their attributes and method
signatures are on the [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work#spring-annotations) page. The lease names they elect (the
`name` of `@SimbaScheduled`, `{group}.{partition}` of `@SimbaPartitioned`) and the groups must be unique across both
annotations: startup fails on a conflict.

## Shutdown Order

1. `SimbaScheduledBeanPostProcessor` (phase `DEFAULT_PHASE`) stops every annotated method: work is interrupted, and
   each lease is released once its work exited (see [Handover Order](/guide/correctness#handover-order)).
2. `SimbaLifecycle` (phase `DEFAULT_PHASE - 4096`) then closes the `Simba` client, which revokes every remaining term,
   closes the session and frees its leases, before lower-phase infrastructure such as connection factories stops.

Elections and locks you started yourself should be stopped before that, e.g. in a `ContextClosedEvent` listener;
closing the client stops them anyway.

## Without Spring

Build the client with `Simba.builder()`:

```kotlin
val simba = Simba.builder()
    .backend(JdbcLeaseBackend.mysql(dataSource, queryTimeout = Duration.ofSeconds(5)))
    .config(SimbaConfig.builder().leaseDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(15)).renewInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).build())
    .listener(myEventListener)
    .build()
```

| Builder method | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `backend(LeaseBackend)` | required | The backend; the client does not close it |
| `config(SimbaConfig)` | `SimbaConfig.builder().build()` | Session timing, see [Timing](/guide/correctness#timing) |
| `listener(SimbaEventListener)` | none | Receives every [`SimbaEvent`](/guide/observability#events); may be called several times |
| `ioExecutor(Executor)` | a virtual thread per call | Runs backend calls |
| `callbackExecutor(Executor)` | virtual threads | Runs leadership callbacks, serially per election |
| `workExecutor(Executor)` | a virtual thread per term | Runs leader work |
| `ticker(Ticker)` | `System.nanoTime()` | Monotonic clock; must advance at the rate of `System.nanoTime()` |
| `seed(Long)` | random | Seed of the retry jitter |

Create **one client per process**. Several clients in one process are several sessions: useful only to isolate
groups of leases from each other's renewal failures, at the cost of one keep-alive each. `close()` (or
`closeAsync()`) revokes every term, closes the session and completes after the last callback ran; close the backend
afterwards.
</doc>

<doc title="Leader Work and Partitions" path="guide/leader-work.md">
# Leader Work and Partitions

Work started through Simba is **bound to one term**: it receives that `Term`, runs only while the term lasts, and is
interrupted when the term ends. It never reads "the current leadership state", so a run that started in one term can
never pick up the token of a later one.

## Run While Leader

```kotlin
val task: LeaderTask = simba.election("ingest").runWhileLeader { term ->
    val cursor = cursors.load()
    while (term.isValid) {
        val batch = source.poll(cursor) ?: continue
        sink.write(batch, fencingToken = term.token)
    }
}
```

- The election starts at once. The block runs once per term, each time on a new virtual thread of the client's work
  executor (or on the `Executor` passed as the first argument).
- When the term is revoked, its thread is interrupted and `term.revoked` completes. Write the block so that it stops on
  interruption or when `term.isValid` turns `false`.
- A block that returns early keeps the term until it ends; the block does not run again until the next term.
- Exceptions are logged and published as `SimbaEvent.WorkCompleted` with outcome `FAILED` (or `CANCELLED` once the term
  has ended); they never affect the election.
- `task.stop()` stops the election and completes once the current work exited (or ran out of time) and the lease is
  released; `task.close()` does the same and waits. See [Handover Order](/guide/correctness#handover-order).

`runWhileLeader` and `schedule` throw `IllegalStateException` when the election is already started on this client.

## Schedules

`schedule` is `runWhileLeader` plus a loop: one loop per term, on one virtual thread, calling `term.ensureValid()`
before every run.

```kotlin
simba.election("report").schedule(
    Schedule.fixedRate(Duration.ofMinutes(1)).withInitialDelay(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
) { term ->
    reportService.generate(fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

| Factory | Period measured |
|---|---|
| `Schedule.fixedDelay(delay, initialDelay = 0)` | From the end of one run to the start of the next |
| `Schedule.fixedRate(period, initialDelay = 0)` | Between scheduled starts; a run that overruns skips the missed starts instead of bursting |

`initialDelay` counts from the start of each term. A failed run (an `Error` included) is logged and published, and the loop goes on; a `VirtualMachineError` ends the loop and steps the election down for one lease duration; the
loop ends with its term. There is no thread pool per schedule.

## Partition Groups

A partition group spreads `partitions` partitions over the live nodes of the group, each partition on exactly one
node at a time:

```kotlin
val task: GroupTask = simba.group("billing", partitions = 16)
    .schedule(Schedule.fixedDelay(Duration.ofMinutes(1))) { term, partition ->
        billing.run(shard = partition, fencingToken = term.token)
    }

task.partitions()   // partitions this node runs in its latest view
```

How it works:

1. The client's session joins the group on the backend; members are the group's live sessions, so membership needs no
   heartbeat of its own and disappears with the session.
2. Every node computes the same assignment from the member list with rendezvous hashing (`PartitionAssignment`, over
   session ids), so adding or removing a node moves only the partitions it gains or loses.
3. Each partition `p` is an ordinary election of the lease `"{group}.{p}"`. A node contends only for the partitions
   assigned to it, and hands over (work first, then the lease) the ones it no longer owns.
4. The member view is refreshed on backend membership hints (Zookeeper) and every renew interval.

The lease guarantees that a partition never has two valid terms at once, even while nodes disagree about the member
list during a change; the assignment only decides who contends. Every member must use the same `partitions`. The
group name follows the lease name rules, and `"{group}.{partitions - 1}"` must fit in 128 characters.

`runWhileLeader { term, partition -> }` is available too. `GroupTask.stop()` leaves the group and stops every
partition, completing once each one handed over, including partitions an earlier view moved away that are still
handing over.

## Spring Annotations

### `@SimbaScheduled`

```java
@Service
public class ReportJobs {
    @SimbaScheduled(name = "report", fixedDelay = "1m", initialDelay = "10s")
    public void generate(Term term) {
        reportService.generate(term.getToken());
    }
}
```

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | Election (lease name) whose leader runs the method; unique per application |
| `fixedDelay` | Delay between the end of one run and the start of the next |
| `fixedRate` | Period between the starts of consecutive runs |
| `initialDelay` | Delay before the first run of each term (default `0s`) |

Set exactly one of `fixedDelay` and `fixedRate`. The method takes no parameter or a single `Term`.

### `@SimbaPartitioned`

```java
@Service
public class Billing {
    @SimbaPartitioned(group = "billing", partitions = 16, fixedDelay = "1m")
    public void bill(Term term, int partition) {
        billing.run(partition, term.getToken());
    }
}
```

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| `group` | Group name, unique per application; partition `p` is elected as `"{group}.{p}"` |
| `partitions` | Number of partitions; every member must use the same value |
| `fixedDelay` / `fixedRate` / `initialDelay` | As for `@SimbaScheduled`, per partition |

The method takes `(Term, int)`.

String attributes of both annotations accept `${...}` placeholders, and durations use the Spring Boot formats (`10s`,
`500ms`, `PT1M`). Methods start after the context refreshed and stop on shutdown before the client closes; see
[Shutdown Order](/guide/configuration#shutdown-order). Disable them with `simba.scheduling.enabled=false`.

## Writing Good Leader Work

- **Pass `term.token` to every write** the work makes to a shared resource. A paused node can still land a write after
  its term ended; only a resource that checks the [fencing token](/guide/correctness#fencing-tokens) rejects it.
- **Stop on interruption.** Blocking I/O that ignores interruption delays the handover up to the term's remaining
  time.
- **Check before long steps:** `term.ensureValid(expectedStepDuration)` throws `TermExpiredException` instead of
  starting a step that would outlive the term.
- **Make work idempotent** where you can: after a failover the next leader may redo the last step.
</doc>

<doc title="Locks" path="guide/locks.md">
# Locks

`simba.lock(name)` holds a lease around a step and releases it afterwards. The lock is an election of the same lease
name that takes its first term and gives it back when you are done.

```kotlin
simba.lock("invoice-42").acquire(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).use { term ->
    term.ensureValid(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
    invoiceStore.write(invoice, fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

```java
try (LockTerm term = simba.lock("invoice-42").acquire(Duration.ofSeconds(5))) {
    term.ensureValid(Duration.ofSeconds(2));
    invoiceStore.write(invoice, term.getToken());
} catch (LockTimeoutException e) {
    // held elsewhere
} catch (InterruptedException e) {
    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
}
```

## Acquiring

| Method | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `acquire(timeout)` | Waits up to `timeout` (on the client's clock) for a term; throws `LockTimeoutException` when none was won in time. A term that ends right after it was won does not end the wait: the lock contends again until the timeout. A timeout too large for nanoseconds waits `Long.MAX_VALUE` ns. Interrupting the caller abandons the attempt and rethrows `InterruptedException` (declared for Java). Calling it on the engine loop (only reachable with a direct callback executor) throws `IllegalStateException`. |
| `tryAcquire()` | One attempt: the term when this client wins the first answered attempt; `null` when another session or this client holds the lease, or when no attempt is answered within one lease duration (backend unreachable). |
| `acquireAsync(timeout)` | `acquire` without blocking (since 5.1): a `CompletionStage<LockTerm>` that completes with the term, or exceptionally with `LockTimeoutException` (timeout), `IllegalStateException` (client closed) or `IllegalArgumentException` (negative timeout); it never throws. |
| `tryAcquireAsync()` | `tryAcquire` without blocking (since 5.1): a `CompletionStage<LockTerm?>` that completes with the term or `null`. |

### Without Blocking

`acquireAsync` and `tryAcquireAsync` wait without a thread and complete on the client's callback executor (on its
event loop only with a direct callback executor, as callbacks do). Their dependents run like callbacks: `close()` on
the term there releases without waiting. A term that ends before the stage could complete with it is never returned:
the lock contends again. **Cancelling** the returned future (`toCompletableFuture().cancel(...)`) abandons the attempt and
releases a term it already won, so a cancelled acquisition never leaves the lock held. Reactor users can wrap the
stage with `Mono.fromCompletionStage`.

```kotlin
simba.lock("invoice-42").acquireAsync(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
    .thenCompose { term ->
        invoiceStore.writeAsync(invoice, fencingToken = term.token)
            .whenComplete { _, _ -> term.releaseAsync() }
    }
```

```java
simba.lock("invoice-42").acquireAsync(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
    .thenCompose(term -> invoiceStore.writeAsync(invoice, term.getToken())
        .whenComplete((result, error) -> term.releaseAsync()));
```

`DistributedLock` implementations other than the client's inherit default methods that run the blocking call on a
virtual thread and interrupt it on cancellation.

### Coroutines

`simba-coroutines` (since 5.1, depends on `kotlinx-coroutines-core`; `simba-core` does not) adapts the async calls:

```kotlin
simba.lock("invoice-42").withLock(Duration.ofSeconds(5)) { term ->
    invoiceStore.write(invoice, fencingToken = term.token)
}
```

| Function | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `DistributedLock.awaitAcquire(timeout)` | Suspends until a term is won; throws `LockTimeoutException`. Cancelling the coroutine abandons the attempt and releases a term it already won. |
| `DistributedLock.awaitTryAcquire()` | `tryAcquireAsync` as a suspending call: the term or `null`. |
| `DistributedLock.withLock(timeout) { term -> }` | Acquires, runs the block and releases the term afterwards, also on failure or cancellation. The term can still end before the block returns: pass `term.token` to the protected resource. |
| `Term.awaitRevoked()` | Suspends until the term is revoked and returns the `RevokeReason`; cancelling the wait does not affect the term. |
| `SimbaEventFlow` | A `SimbaEventListener` to register with `Simba.builder().listener(...)`; `events` is a hot `SharedFlow<SimbaEvent>` that drops the oldest events for a collector more than `bufferCapacity` behind. |

Within one client a name has **at most one holder**: a second `acquire` of the same name waits until the first is
released (or its own timeout passes). A lock and an election of the same name share one lease, so do not use one
name for both.

## The `LockTerm` Is the Credential

`acquire` returns a `LockTerm`: a [`Term`](/guide/correctness#leases-terms-and-tokens) that also releases the lease.

- It is **not bound to a thread**: hand it to another thread or coroutine and close it there.
- `close()` revokes the term and releases the lease, and waits for that (except inside a leadership callback or leader
  work). `releaseAsync()` does the same without waiting. Both are idempotent.
- `token`, `isValid`, `remaining()` and `ensureValid()` behave as for any term.

## Losing a Lock Early

A held lock ends before you close it when its term is revoked: the session's local deadline passed, the backend
reported the session expired, or another session took the lease over. The lock is then **released for good**, not
re-acquired behind your back:

- `term.isValid` turns `false` and `term.revoked` completes with the reason;
- your next `ensureValid()` throws `TermExpiredException`;
- closing the `LockTerm` afterwards is a harmless no-op.

Because a lock can end while your code still runs, pass `term.token` to the protected resource and let it reject
lower tokens; see [Fencing Tokens](/guide/correctness#fencing-tokens). Use `ensureValid(expectedStepDuration)`
before each step so that you do not start a step the term cannot cover.

## Choosing Between a Lock and an Election

| | Lock | Election |
|---|---|---|
| Lifetime | Around one step, released by you | As long as the election runs |
| Ends early | Released for good | Contends again for the next term |
| Typical use | Mutually exclusive access to one resource | A role one node plays continuously |

For periodic or continuous work on one node, use [leader work](/guide/leader-work) instead of a lock in a loop: it
contends once and keeps the term between runs.
</doc>

<doc title="Observability" path="guide/observability.md">
# Observability

Simba reports what it does in two ways: a point-in-time `snapshot()` of the session and every election, and a stream
of `SimbaEvent`s. The Spring Boot starter builds the Actuator endpoint and the health indicator on the snapshot, and
the Micrometer metrics on the events.

## Snapshot

`simba.snapshot()` returns a `SimbaSnapshot` read on the engine's loop; it never calls the backend.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `session.id` | The current `SessionId`, `null` while none is open |
| `session.status` | `OPENING`, `LIVE`, `SUSPENDED` or `CLOSED` |
| `session.validFor` | Time left before the session's local deadline |
| `session.notLiveFor` | How long the session has not been `LIVE` (since start, or since it was last live); zero while live |
| `elections[]` | Every started election (locks, schedules and partitions included): `name`, `status`, `token`, `remaining`, `kind` (`ELECTION`, `LOCK` or `GROUP`: which API started it) |
| `leaseDuration` | The configured session lease |
| `healthy` | `notLiveFor ≤ leaseDuration` |

An election's `status` is `CANDIDATE` (contending), `LEADER` (holding a valid term), `COOLDOWN` (stepped down, waiting
for the cooldown to end) or `HANDOVER` (stopped or stepped down, waiting for its work to exit before releasing the
lease). `token` and `remaining` are `0` without a term.

## Events

Register a `SimbaEventListener` with `Simba.builder().listener(...)`, or as a bean with the starter. Events are
delivered in order on one serial dispatcher over the callback executor, never on the engine's loop, so a listener may
call `snapshot()`, `stop()` and other client APIs; blocking `close()` methods do not wait when called from a listener.
`close()` completes after the last event was delivered. Keep listeners fast; exceptions are logged and ignored. Events
are plain classes with value equality (no `copy` or destructuring), so later versions can add properties.

| `SimbaEvent` | When |
|---|---|
| `SessionOpened(session)` | A new session was opened |
| `SessionRenewed(session, latency)` | A keep-alive succeeded |
| `SessionSuspended(session, cause)` | A keep-alive failed before the local deadline |
| `SessionExpired(session, reason)` | The session ended: `reason` is `DEADLINE_PASSED` (no keep-alive succeeded before the local deadline) or `SESSION_EXPIRED` (the backend reported it expired) |
| `SessionLeaseShortened(session, remaining, renewEvery)` | The backend grants less than the configured lease (e.g. a capped Zookeeper session timeout), so the client renews every `renewEvery` (a third of the local validity) instead; once per session, also logged as a warning |
| `SessionClosed(session)` | The client closed (`session` is `null` when none was open); published once |
| `Elected(name, token, kind)` | This node got a term; `kind` (`ELECTION`, `LOCK`, `GROUP`) tells which API started the election, so metrics can label by kind instead of by unbounded lock names |
| `Revoked(name, token, reason, kind)` | A term ended |
| `AcquireFailed(name, cause, kind)` | An acquire call failed (not "held by someone else", which is normal) |
| `WorkCompleted(name, token, outcome, duration, cause, kind)` | One run of leader work ended: `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED` |

```kotlin
@Component
class AuditListener(private val audit: Audit) : SimbaEventListener {
    override fun onEvent(event: SimbaEvent) {
        when (event) {
            is SimbaEvent.Elected -> audit.record("leader", event.name.value, event.token)
            is SimbaEvent.Revoked -> audit.record("revoked", event.name.value, event.reason)
            else -> Unit
        }
    }
}
```

## Micrometer Metrics

With Micrometer on the classpath and a `MeterRegistry` bean, the starter registers `MicrometerSimbaEventListener`
(disable with `simba.metrics.enabled=false`):

| Meter | Type | Tags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `simba.session.renew` | Timer | — | Latency of successful keep-alives |
| `simba.session.state` | Gauge | `state` (`opening`, `live`, `suspended`, `closed`) | `1` for the current session status |
| `simba.leadership` | Gauge | `name` | `1` while this node holds a term of the election or partition, `0` after it lost one |
| `simba.locks.held` | Gauge | — | Locks this node holds |
| `simba.revocations` | Counter | `reason`, `kind` (`election`, `lock`, `group`) | Ended terms, by `RevokeReason` (lowercase), including `stopped` and `stepped_down` |
| `simba.work` | Timer | `name`, `outcome` | Leader work runs (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`) |

Only elections and partitions (`{group}.{partition}`), whose names come from your code, are tagged by name. Locks,
whose names often come from data (`invoice-42`), are counted together: `simba.locks.held` and the `kind="lock"`
revocations, so a normal unlock never reads as "no leader". A name's `simba.leadership` series exists from its first
term until a term ends `stopped` (the election stopped, the partition moved to another node, or the client closed), so
stopped elections leave no series behind. Without Spring, add
`MicrometerSimbaEventListener(registry)` to the builder yourself.

## Alert Rules

Prometheus examples (Micrometer renders dots as underscores):

```yaml
groups:
  - name: simba
    rules:
      - alert: SimbaNoLeader
        expr: sum by (name) (simba_leadership) < 1
        for: 1m
        annotations:
          summary: "No node leads {{ $labels.name }}"
      - alert: SimbaSessionNotLive
        expr: simba_session_state{state="live"} == 0
        for: 1m
        annotations:
          summary: "The Simba session of {{ $labels.instance }} is not live"
      - alert: SimbaTermsLost
        expr: increase(simba_revocations_total{reason=~"deadline_passed|session_expired|taken_over"}[10m]) > 0
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.instance }} lost a {{ $labels.kind }} term ({{ $labels.reason }}); protect writes with fencing tokens"
      - alert: SimbaLeadershipFlapping
        expr: increase(simba_revocations_total{kind!="lock", reason!~"stopped|stepped_down"}[10m]) > 3
        annotations:
          summary: "Leadership on {{ $labels.instance }} moves too often"
      - alert: SimbaWorkFailing
        expr: increase(simba_work_seconds_count{outcome="failed"}[10m]) > 0
        annotations:
          summary: "Leader work of {{ $labels.name }} failed"
```

Nodes are scraped at different moments, so a handover can briefly look like zero or two leaders; the `for: 1m`
clause filters that out. `simba_leadership` is each node's local view: two nodes reporting `1` for longer than a lease
point at a paused node or a backend that lost writes (for example a Redis failover), which is exactly what
[fencing tokens](/guide/correctness#fencing-tokens) protect against.

## Actuator Endpoint

With Spring Boot Actuator, the read-only `simba` endpoint shows the snapshot. Like every Actuator endpoint it is not
exposed over HTTP by default:

```yaml
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,simba
```

`GET /actuator/simba`:

```json
{
  "session": {
    "id": "5f0c8e9d2b7a4c1e9f3a6b8d0e2c4a71",
    "status": "LIVE",
    "validForMillis": 13870,
    "notLiveForMillis": 0
  },
  "elections": [
    { "name": "report", "status": "LEADER", "token": 42, "remainingMillis": 13870, "kind": "ELECTION" },
    { "name": "billing.3", "status": "CANDIDATE", "token": 0, "remainingMillis": 0, "kind": "GROUP" }
  ]
}
```

`GET /actuator/simba/{name}` returns one election, or `404` when it is not started on this node. The endpoint shows
only this node's view; it does not query who leads elsewhere.

## Health Indicator

The `simba` health indicator is `DOWN` once the session has not been live for longer than `leaseDuration`: this node
can then neither keep nor win a term on any backend. Not leading is healthy. `leading` lists the elections and
partitions this node leads; locks are only counted (`locksHeld`), because their names come from data.

```json
{
  "status": "UP",
  "details": {
    "session": "5f0c8e9d2b7a4c1e9f3a6b8d0e2c4a71",
    "status": "LIVE",
    "validFor": "13870ms",
    "notLiveFor": "0ms",
    "leaseDuration": "15000ms",
    "leading": ["report"],
    "locksHeld": 1
  }
}
```

The indicator is **not** part of the liveness or readiness groups. A backend outage hits every node at once;
restarting or unrouting all of them would turn a coordination outage into an application outage. Add it to a group
yourself (`management.endpoint.health.group.<name>.include=simba`) only if that is what you want, and disable it with
`management.health.simba.enabled=false`.

## Related Pages

- [Spring Boot](/guide/configuration): every `simba.*` property and the beans the starter creates.
- [Concepts and Correctness](/guide/correctness#failure-modes): what each failure looks like.
</doc>

<doc title="Testing" path="guide/testing.md">
# Testing

Two test modules help you test code built on Simba and code Simba depends on:

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| `simba-testing` | `InMemoryLeaseBackend`, `VirtualClock`, `VirtualScheduler`, `Simulation` |
| `simba-tck` | `FencingSpec` (for your token-checking resource) and `LeaseBackendSpec` (for a backend) |

```kotlin
testImplementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-testing:${simbaVersion}")
testImplementation("me.ahoo.simba:simba-tck:${simbaVersion}")
```

The examples assert with [FluentAssert](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/FluentAssert) (`.assert()`), which `simba-tck`
brings in; with `simba-testing` alone, add `me.ahoo.test:fluent-assert-core` or use your own assertion library.

## In-Memory Backend

`InMemoryLeaseBackend` implements the full `LeaseBackend` contract in memory (sessions, leases with never-resetting
tokens, groups, release and membership hints). It needs no infrastructure, so it fits unit tests of anything that
takes a `Simba`:

```kotlin
@Test
fun `only one client leads`() {
    val backend = InMemoryLeaseBackend()
    val config = SimbaConfig.builder().leaseDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(3)).renewInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(1)).build()
    Simba.builder().backend(backend).config(config).build().use { first ->
        Simba.builder().backend(backend).config(config).build().use { second ->
            val elected = LinkedBlockingQueue<Term>()
            val listener = object : LeadershipListener {
                override fun onElected(term: Term) { elected += term }
                override fun onRevoked(term: Term, reason: RevokeReason) = Unit
            }
            first.election("job").start(listener)
            second.election("job").start(listener)

            val term = elected.poll(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)!!
            backend.owner(term.name)!!.token.assert().isEqualTo(term.token)
        }
    }
}
```

`owner(name)` and `token(name)` let a test inspect the backend directly. Wait on queues, latches or futures, never
`sleep`.

In a Spring Boot test, define the backend as a bean: the starter builds the `Simba` client over any `LeaseBackend`
bean, with no backend module on the test classpath.

```kotlin
@TestConfiguration
class InMemorySimba {
    @Bean
    fun leaseBackend(): LeaseBackend = InMemoryLeaseBackend()
}
```

## Virtual Time

With the in-memory backend on real time, a test of a failover still waits for a lease to expire. To run such tests
instantly and deterministically, drive the client and the backend from one `VirtualScheduler`:

```kotlin
@OptIn(InternalSimbaApi::class)
class FailoverTest {
    private val scheduler = VirtualScheduler()
    private val backend = InMemoryLeaseBackend(scheduler)

    private fun client(): Simba = Simba.builder()
        .backend(backend)
        .config(SimbaConfig.builder().leaseDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(3)).renewInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(1)).build())
        .scheduler(scheduler)          // clock and timers of the engine
        .ioExecutor(Runnable::run)     // backend calls inline
        .callbackExecutor(Runnable::run)
        .seed(0)
        .build()

    private fun advance(duration: Duration, vararg clients: Simba) =
        scheduler.advance(duration) { clients.forEach { it.awaitIdle() } }
}
```

`scheduler.advance(duration, settle)` moves virtual time forward and fires every due timer in order, calling `settle`
before each so that what a timer triggers completes before time moves on. Leader work still runs on its own (virtual)
threads; wait for what it does through queues.

`Simba.Builder.scheduler`, `Simba.awaitIdle` and `Scheduler` are marked `@InternalSimbaApi`: they need an explicit
opt-in and carry no compatibility guarantee between minor versions. `VirtualClock` alone is a plain `Ticker` for code
that only reads time.

## Deterministic Simulation

`Simulation(seed, params).run()` runs several engines against the in-memory backend in virtual time while injecting
message delays and loss, process pauses and clock drift up to `drift`, groups joined and left (partition elections
follow each node's view), nodes closed mid-fault, grants reported shorter than granted, and backend-side faults (a
session expired or a lease deleted by the backend on its own). It checks the invariants: at most one valid term per
name (partitions included) at any moment, strictly increasing tokens, paired callbacks, liveness after faults stop,
and the handover order; terms a backend-side fault removed are exempt from the first two until revoked, since such a
fault breaks the backend's contract. `SimulationParams.builder()` sets the knobs, and `SimulationResult.events`
counts the events and the exercised paths (`path:*`). Simba runs it over 10⁴ seeds in its own build; it is available to anyone changing the engine, and a failing seed
replays exactly:

```bash
./gradlew simba-testing:test -Psimba.simulation.seed=42
```

## Verifying a Fencing Resource

`FencingSpec` checks a resource that guards its writes with fencing tokens (see
[Checking Tokens in the Resource](/guide/correctness#checking-tokens-in-the-resource)). Extend it and implement two
methods:

```kotlin
class LedgerFencingTest : FencingSpec() {
    override fun write(resource: String, fencingToken: Long): Boolean = ledger.settle(resource, fencingToken)
    override fun highestToken(resource: String): Long = ledger.fencingToken(resource)

    // optional: also write with real terms of a backend
    override fun leaseBackend(): LeaseBackend = InMemoryLeaseBackend()
}
```

| Test | Verifies |
|---|---|
| `acceptsIncreasingTokens` | Increasing tokens are accepted |
| `acceptsTheSameTokenAgain` | A retry within one term (same token) is accepted |
| `rejectsLowerToken` | A lower token is rejected and the highest stays |
| `concurrentWritersNeverLetALowerTokenWin` | Racing writers: the highest token always ends up winning |
| `staleTermIsRejectedAfterTheLockMovedOn` | With `leaseBackend()`: a closed lock term's token is rejected once a newer term wrote |

## Backend TCK

`LeaseBackendSpec` is the contract every `LeaseBackend` must pass: mutual exclusion, strictly increasing tokens that
survive release, expired sessions that stay expired, stale releases that are no-ops, batch acquire, group members that
are only live sessions. Extend it for a backend of your own:

```kotlin
class MyLeaseBackendTest : LeaseBackendSpec() {
    override fun createBackend(): LeaseBackend = MyLeaseBackend(connection)

    // optional: a backend with an injectable clock moves it instead of waiting
    override val clock: ClockControl? = null
    override val shortLease: Duration = Duration.ofSeconds(1)
}
```

| Override | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `createBackend()` | required | A new backend over the store under test; closed after each test |
| `lease` | 30 s | Lease of sessions that must outlive a test |
| `shortLease` | 1 s | Lease of sessions a test lets expire; keep it short on real time |
| `clock` | `null` | The backend's clock when the test controls it; otherwise time-based tests poll until the lease ran out |
| `timeout` | 30 s | Upper bound for anything a test waits for |

Every test uses fresh lease and group names, so the store may be shared across tests. The JDBC, Redis and Zookeeper
backends run this spec in Simba's own build; see [Contributing](/contributing/#adding-a-backend).
</doc>

<doc title="Upgrading" path="guide/upgrading.md">
# Upgrading

Simba follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) at the source level: within a major version, code that
compiled against an earlier release compiles against a later one unchanged, so recompile when you upgrade. Binary
compatibility (running code compiled against another release without recompiling) is not promised. Source-breaking
changes of the following only happen in a major version:

| Area | Covered |
|---|---|
| Core API | Public types of `me.ahoo.simba`, `me.ahoo.simba.partition`, `me.ahoo.simba.event`, `me.ahoo.simba.spi` |
| Backends | Public classes of `simba-jdbc`, `simba-redis`, `simba-spring-redis`, `simba-zookeeper` (`JdbcLeaseBackend`, `Dialect`, `RedisLeaseBackend`, `RedisScripting`, `SpringRedisScripting`, `ZookeeperLeaseBackend`, ...) |
| Spring Boot starter | Public types and annotations (`@SimbaScheduled`, `@SimbaPartitioned`, the `*Properties` classes, `SimbaLifecycle`, `MicrometerSimbaEventListener`, `SimbaEndpoint`, `SimbaHealthIndicator`), the `simba.*` properties, bean names and conditions |
