| Coroutines | `simba-coroutines` (since 5.1): the functions and types of `me.ahoo.simba.coroutines` (`awaitAcquire`, `awaitTryAcquire`, `withLock`, `awaitRevoked`, `SimbaEventFlow`) |
| Test kits | `simba-testing` (`InMemoryLeaseBackend`, `VirtualClock`, `VirtualScheduler`, `Simulation`) and `simba-tck` (`LeaseBackendSpec`, `FencingSpec`) |
| Observability | Metric names and tag keys, the Actuator endpoint's and the health indicator's JSON fields |
| Storage | The JDBC schema, the Redis keys and messages, the Zookeeper paths |

New fields, tags, enum constants and events may be added in a minor version: read JSON and handle `when` over Simba
enums and events tolerantly. Types marked `@InternalSimbaApi` (the engine, `Simba.Builder.scheduler`,
`Simba.awaitIdle`) and anything `internal` carry no guarantee.

## From 4.x

5.0 is not compatible with 4.x in API, configuration or storage, and needs every node stopped before the switch. Follow
[Migrating from 4.x to 5.0](/guide/migration).

## Within 5.x

Minor and patch releases keep the storage format, so nodes of different 5.x versions can contend for the same names
and you can roll an upgrade node by node. Release notes list every change:
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/releases).

### 5.0 to 5.1 {#from-5-0-to-5-1}

5.1 only adds API and keeps 5.0's storage, so nodes of both versions can run side by side:

- `DistributedLock.acquireAsync(timeout)` and `tryAcquireAsync()` acquire a lock without blocking; see
  [Locks](/guide/locks#without-blocking). They are default methods, so your own `DistributedLock` implementations
  keep compiling unchanged.
- The new optional module `simba-coroutines` adds suspending lock calls, `withLock`, `Term.awaitRevoked()` and
  `SimbaEventFlow`; it depends on `kotlinx-coroutines-core`, which `simba-core` does not.
</doc>

<doc title="Migrating from 4.x to 5.0" path="guide/migration.md">
# Migrating from 4.x to 5.0

Simba 5 is a rewrite ([ADR 0010](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-simba-5-target-architecture.md)):
one session per process instead of one lease per mutex, a `Term` object instead of owner state, and one engine for
all three backends. It is **not compatible** with 4.x in source, in binary, or on the wire:

- the JDBC tables, Redis keys and Zookeeper paths are different, so a 4.x node and a 5.x node do not see each other's
  leases and would both lead;
- the configuration properties and the Spring beans are different;
- Java 21 is required, and the starter needs Spring Boot 4.1 or later;
- the Redis backend is split: `simba-redis` alone only defines the `RedisScripting` port and cannot run. Depend on
  `simba-spring-redis` (Spring Data Redis with Lettuce, which brings `simba-redis`), or implement `RedisScripting` for
  another client.

You therefore cannot roll the upgrade node by node. **Stop every node that contends for the same names, then start
them on 5.0.** If a short double run would be harmful, make sure no 4.x node is running before the first 5.0 node
starts.

## Steps

1. Update the code with the [API mapping](#api-mapping) below and the configuration with the
   [property mapping](#property-mapping).
2. Prepare the backend:
   - **JDBC:** create the 5.x tables with
     [`init-simba-mysql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-mysql.sql)
     or
     [`init-simba-postgresql.sql`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/simba-jdbc/src/main/resources/me/ahoo/simba/jdbc/init-simba-postgresql.sql).
     The 4.x table `simba_member(group_name, member_id, expire_at)` has the same name as the 5.x table
     `simba_member(group_name, session_id)` but different columns, and the scripts use `create table if not exists`:
     **drop or rename the 4.x `simba_member` first**, or use a separate database or schema.
   - **Redis, Zookeeper:** nothing to create. The 5.x keys and nodes do not overlap the 4.x ones, except that 4.x
     latch nodes also live under `/simba`; a 4.x mutex named `leases` or `groups` collides with the 5.x
     subtrees, so remove the old nodes or set `simba.zookeeper.root` to another path.
3. Stop every 4.x node.
4. Start the 5.0 nodes.
5. Remove the 4.x storage once you no longer need to roll back: table `simba_mutex` (and the 4.x `simba_member`),
   keys `simba:{mutex}`, `simba:{mutex}:fence`, `simba:{mutex}:token`, `simba:{group}:members`, Zookeeper nodes
   `/simba/{mutex}` and `/simba-members`.

Fencing tokens restart: 5.x tokens come from the new storage and start at `1` (Zookeeper: the new nodes' `czxid`). A
resource that recorded 4.x tokens would reject the first 5.x writes; reset its highest token during the switch, or
start the 5.x tokens above it (for JDBC, by inserting `simba_lease` rows with a higher `token` and an empty
`session_id` before the first start).

## API Mapping

| 4.x | 5.0 |
|---|---|
| `MutexContendServiceFactory` + `MutexContender` + `start()` | `simba.election(name).start(listener)` |
| `AbstractMutexContender.onAcquired(mutexState)` / `onReleased(mutexState)` | `LeadershipListener.onElected(term)` / `onRevoked(term, reason)` |
| `MutexContendService.stop()` | `election.stop()` (a `CompletionStage`) |
| `relinquish(cooldown)` | `election.stepDown(cooldown)` |
| `MutexOwner` / `MutexState` | `Term` (this node's term); no view of other nodes' ownership |
| `fencingToken`, `leaseRemaining`, `ensureLease()` on services, lockers, schedulers, contexts | `term.token`, `term.remaining()`, `term.ensureValid()` on the `Term` the work received |
| `isOwner`, `hasOwner()` | `term.isValid`; `simba.snapshot()` for this node's elections |
| `contenderId` (reused across restarts) | `SessionId` (unique per incarnation, never reused) |
| `SimbaLocker(mutex, factory).acquire(timeout)` | `simba.lock(name).acquire(timeout)` returning a `LockTerm` |
| `SimbaScheduler` / `AbstractScheduler` + `ScheduleConfig.delay/rate` | `election.schedule(Schedule.fixedDelay/fixedRate) { term -> }` |
| `ScheduleContext` | The `Term` passed to the work |
| `SimbaPartitionedScheduler` + `MemberRegistry` | `simba.group(name, partitions).schedule { term, partition -> }` |
| `PartitionContext` | `(term, partition)` |
| `@SimbaScheduled(mutex = ..., worker = ...)` with `ScheduleContext` | `@SimbaScheduled(name = ...)` with `Term` |
| — | `@SimbaPartitioned(group, partitions, ...)` with `(Term, Int)` |
| `ContendObserver` | `SimbaEventListener` receiving `SimbaEvent`s |
| `MutexLeaseStore`, `MutexOwnerRepository`, `MemberRegistry` (SPIs) | `LeaseBackend` |
| `JdbcMutexContendServiceFactory` | `JdbcLeaseBackend.mysql(dataSource)` / `postgres(dataSource)` |
| `SpringRedisMutexContendServiceFactory` | `RedisLeaseBackend(SpringRedisScripting(connectionFactory))` |
| `ZookeeperMutexContendServiceFactory` (Curator `LeaderLatch`) | `ZookeeperLeaseBackend(connectString)` (ephemeral nodes) |
| `MutexContendServiceSpec`, `LockSpec`, `MemberRegistrySpec` (`simba-test`) | `LeaseBackendSpec` (`simba-tck`) |
| `FencingSpec` (`simba-test`) | `FencingSpec` (`simba-tck`) |
| — | `simba-testing`: `InMemoryLeaseBackend`, `VirtualScheduler`, `Simulation` |
| `Simba` (the 4.x constants object `SIMBA`, `SIMBA_PREFIX`) | `Simba` is now the client class (`Simba.builder()`); the constants are gone |
| `MutexRetriever`, `MutexRetrievalService`, `AbstractMutexRetrievalService` (observers) | No equivalent: a node sees only its own terms. Query `simba.snapshot()` for this node's elections, or read the backend's storage (see [Backends](/guide/backends)) to see who holds a lease |
| `Locker` (interface of `SimbaLocker`) | `DistributedLock` (`simba.lock(name)`), whose `acquire` returns a `LockTerm` |
| `LeaseConfig` (`ttl`, `transition`) | `SimbaConfig` (`leaseDuration`, `renewInterval`, `drift`, `margin`), one per client |
| `ContenderIdGenerator` | Removed: the backend issues a `SessionId` per session |
| `MicrometerContendObserver` | `MicrometerSimbaEventListener` |
| `SimbaServiceTracker` (Actuator) | Removed: the endpoint reads `simba.snapshot()` |
| `ScheduledWork` / `PartitionedWork` | `LeaderWork` (`run(term)`) / `PartitionWork` (`run(term, partition)`) |
| `me.ahoo.simba.core.LeaseExpiredException` | `me.ahoo.simba.TermExpiredException`, thrown by `Term.ensureValid` |

Behavior that changed:

- **Every term is a new object.** A callback or a work block only ever sees its own term, so it cannot read a later
  term's token by accident.
- **One session per node.** One keep-alive renews every lease and membership; one renewal failure affects them all.
  Create several `Simba` clients if you need isolation.
- **Locks are not bound to threads.** A `LockTerm` may be closed from any thread; a lock lost early is not
  re-acquired.
- **No push of other nodes' ownership.** 4.x notified every contender of other nodes' acquisitions; 5.x reports only
  this node's terms.
- **Zookeeper leases are bounded** like the others: `remaining()` has the same meaning on all three backends, and
  FIFO fairness of `LeaderLatch` is gone.
- **Leader work runs on virtual threads**, one per term; there is no thread pool per scheduler.

### Removed Internals

These 4.x public types were implementation details; 5.0 has no replacement to code against. Configure a backend
(`JdbcLeaseBackend`, `RedisLeaseBackend`, `ZookeeperLeaseBackend`) and use `Simba` instead:

| Module | 4.x types | 5.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `simba-core` | `AbstractMutexContendService`, `LeaseContendService`, `ContendPeriod`, `ContendExecutors`, `ContendOutcome` | The engine (internal); executors are set on `Simba.builder()`, outcomes are `SimbaEvent`s |
| `simba-core` | `UUIDContenderIdGenerator`, `HostContenderIdGenerator` | None: the backend issues a `SessionId` per session |
| `simba-jdbc` | `JdbcMutexContendService`, `JdbcMutexOwnerRepository`, `JdbcMemberRegistry`, `NotFoundMutexOwnerException` | `JdbcLeaseBackend` |
| `simba-spring-redis` | `SpringRedisMutexContendService`, `SpringRedisMemberRegistry`, `OwnerEvent` | `RedisLeaseBackend` over `SpringRedisScripting`; release hints replace the owner events |
| `simba-zookeeper` | `ZookeeperMutexContendService`, `ZookeeperMemberRegistry` | `ZookeeperLeaseBackend` |
| `simba-spring-boot-starter` | `SimbaSpringRedisAutoConfiguration` | `SimbaRedisAutoConfiguration` |

## Property Mapping

| 4.x | 5.0 |
|---|---|
| `simba.enabled`, `simba.backend`, `simba.<backend>.enabled` | Unchanged |
| `simba.jdbc.ttl`, `simba.redis.ttl` + `transition` | `simba.session.lease-duration` and `simba.session.renew-interval`, for every backend |
| `simba.jdbc.initial-delay` | Removed |
| `simba.jdbc.fencing` | Removed: tokens are always on |
| — | `simba.session.drift`, `simba.session.margin` |
| — | `simba.jdbc.dialect`, `simba.jdbc.query-timeout` |
| — | `simba.redis.wait-replicas`, `simba.redis.wait-timeout`, `simba.redis.route-by-slot` |
| `CuratorFramework` bean (Zookeeper) | `simba.zookeeper.connect-string`, `root`, `connection-timeout` |
| `simba.scheduling.enabled`, `simba.metrics.enabled` | Unchanged |

As a starting point, `lease-duration ≈ ttl + transition` keeps the failover time of 4.x.

## Storage Mapping

| | 4.x | 5.0 |
|---|---|---|
| JDBC | `simba_mutex` (one row per mutex), `simba_member(group_name, member_id, expire_at)` | `simba_session`, `simba_lease`, `simba_member(group_name, session_id)` |
| Redis | `simba:{mutex}`, `simba:{mutex}:fence`, `simba:{mutex}:token`, `simba:{group}:members`, channel `simba:{mutex}` | `simba:lease:{name}`, `simba:session:{sid}` (+ `:leases`, `:groups`), `simba:group:{group}` |
| Zookeeper | `LeaderLatch` at `/simba/{mutex}`, members `/simba-members/{group}/{memberId}` | `/simba/leases/{name}`, `/simba/groups/{group}/{sessionId}` |

Partition leases keep the `{group}.{partition}` names and the same rendezvous weights, but members are now session
ids, so the assignment of partitions to nodes changes.

## Metrics and Endpoint Mapping

| 4.x | 5.0 |
|---|---|
| `simba.mutex.owner{mutex}` | `simba.leadership{name}` |
| `simba.mutex.ownership.changes{mutex,change}` | `simba.revocations{reason,kind}` (every ended term, `stopped` and `stepped_down` included); locks: `simba.locks.held` |
| `simba.mutex.contend{mutex,operation,outcome}` | `simba.session.renew` (one keep-alive per node) |
| `simba.mutex.lease.expired{mutex}` | `simba.revocations{reason="deadline_passed"}` |
| `simba.scheduler.work{mutex,outcome}` | `simba.work{name,outcome}` |
| — | `simba.session.state{state}` |
| `/actuator/simba` per mutex and contender | `/actuator/simba`: session plus elections, from `snapshot()` |
| `simba` health: stale contenders | `simba` health: session not live for longer than the lease |

Update dashboards and the [alert rules](/guide/observability#alert-rules) accordingly.
</doc>

<doc title="API Reference" path="api/index.md">
# API Reference

Public API lives in `me.ahoo.simba` (`simba-core`) and its subpackages `partition`, `event` and `spi`. Times are always
`java.time.Duration`. Types in `me.ahoo.simba.engine` and members marked `@InternalSimbaApi` require an opt-in and are
not public API.

## Client — `me.ahoo.simba`

### `Simba`

One client per process: one backend session, with every election, lock and group attached to it. `AutoCloseable`.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `Simba.builder()` | Builder; see [Without Spring](/guide/configuration#without-spring) |
| `config: SimbaConfig` | The session timing |
| `election(name): Election` | The election of `name`; handles of the same name share one election |
| `lock(name): DistributedLock` | The lock on `name`; a lock and an election of the same name share one lease |
| `group(name, partitions): PartitionGroup` | The partition group `name` with `partitions` partitions |
| `snapshot(): SimbaSnapshot` | The session and every started election, without calling the backend |
| `closeAsync(): CompletionStage<Void>` | Revokes every term, closes the session; completes after the last callback ran |
| `close()` | `closeAsync()` and wait, except inside a callback or leader work |

Names follow the lease name rules: 1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; anything else throws
`IllegalArgumentException`. After `close()`, every method that starts something throws `IllegalStateException`.

### `SimbaConfig`

`SimbaConfig.builder()` with `leaseDuration` (15s), `renewInterval` (`leaseDuration / 3`), `drift` (0.01), `margin`
(50ms), `retryJitter` (`renewInterval / 2`), `minBackoff` (100ms); unset values keep their defaults, derived ones
follow the values set. `build()` validates `renewInterval × 2 ≤ leaseDuration` and
`leaseDuration × (1 − drift) − margin > renewInterval`; `toBuilder()` derives a variant. There is no public
constructor: `SimbaConfig`, the events and the snapshots are plain classes with value equality (no `copy` or
destructuring), so later versions can add properties compatibly. See
[Timing](/guide/correctness#timing).

## Elections — `me.ahoo.simba`

### `Election`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `name: LeaseName` | The lease name |
| `start(listener)` | Starts contending; throws `IllegalStateException` when already started |
| `stop(): CompletionStage<Void>` | Stops contending; completes after the last `onRevoked` ran (at once when not started) |
| `stepDown(cooldown): CompletionStage<Void>` | Gives up the current term and does not contend for `cooldown`; stays started |
| `runWhileLeader(executor?, work): LeaderTask` | Starts the election and runs `work` once per term |
| `schedule(schedule, work): LeaderTask` | Starts the election and runs `work` on `schedule` while leader |

Contract: every `onElected(term)` is followed by exactly one `onRevoked(term, reason)`; callbacks of one election run
one at a time, in order; the engine never waits for a callback except through the futures of `stop()` and
`stepDown()`; after `stop()` completed, no more callbacks.

### `LeadershipListener`

```kotlin
interface LeadershipListener {
    fun onElected(term: Term)
    fun onRevoked(term: Term, reason: RevokeReason)
}
```

### `LeaderWork` and `LeaderTask`

`fun interface LeaderWork { fun run(term: Term) }` may throw anything; failures (an `Error` included) become
`SimbaEvent.WorkCompleted` and never affect the election, except a `VirtualMachineError` (out of memory, stack
overflow): it ends the term's work, the election steps down for one lease duration, and the error is rethrown to the
work thread. `LeaderTask` (`AutoCloseable`) exposes `election`, `stop(): CompletionStage<Void>` (completes once
the work exited or timed out and the lease is released) and `close()`. See [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work).

### `Schedule`

`Schedule.fixedDelay(delay, initialDelay = 0)`, `Schedule.fixedRate(period, initialDelay = 0)`,
`withInitialDelay(initialDelay)`; `mode`, `period`, `initialDelay`. The period must be positive. A fixed-rate run that
overruns skips the missed starts.

## Terms — `me.ahoo.simba`

### `Term`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `name: LeaseName` | The lease name |
| `token: Long` | Fencing token: `> 0`, constant within the term, strictly increasing across terms of the name |
| `isValid: Boolean` | Not revoked and the session's local deadline has not passed |
| `remaining(): Duration` | Time left before the local deadline; `ZERO` once the term ended |
| `ensureValid(minRemaining)`, `ensureValid()` | Throws `TermExpiredException` unless valid for more than `minRemaining` (`ZERO` without an argument) |
| `revoked: CompletionStage<RevokeReason>` | Completes exactly once, when the term is revoked |

### `RevokeReason`

`STOPPED`, `STEPPED_DOWN`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `DEADLINE_PASSED`, `TAKEN_OVER`; see
[Leases, Terms and Tokens](/guide/correctness#leases-terms-and-tokens).

## Locks — `me.ahoo.simba`

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `DistributedLock` | `name`; `acquire(timeout): LockTerm` (throws `LockTimeoutException`; declares `InterruptedException`); `tryAcquire(): LockTerm?`; since 5.1 `acquireAsync(timeout): CompletionStage<LockTerm>` and `tryAcquireAsync(): CompletionStage<LockTerm?>` (cancelling abandons the attempt and releases a won term) |
| `LockTerm : Term, AutoCloseable` | `releaseAsync(): CompletionStage<Void>`; `close()` (idempotent) |
| `LockTimeoutException` | `name`, `timeout` |

See [Locks](/guide/locks).

## Partitions — `me.ahoo.simba.partition`

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `PartitionGroup` | `name` (a `String`: it names a backend membership group, not a lease, yet follows the lease-name rules), `partitions`; `schedule(schedule, work): GroupTask`; `runWhileLeader(work): GroupTask` |
| `PartitionWork` | `fun run(term: Term, partition: Int)` |
| `GroupTask : AutoCloseable` | `group`; `partitions(): Set<Int>` (this node's partitions in its latest view); `stop()`; `close()` |
| `PartitionAssignment` | `ownerOf(partition, members)`, `partitionsOf(member, partitions, members)`, `weight(partition, member)`: rendezvous hashing (FNV-1a 64 mixed with SplitMix64), identical across versions |

## Events and Snapshot — `me.ahoo.simba.event`

| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| `SimbaEventListener` | `fun onEvent(event: SimbaEvent)`; called in order off the engine loop; exceptions are logged and ignored |
| `SimbaEvent` | `SessionOpened`, `SessionRenewed`, `SessionSuspended`, `SessionExpired` (`reason`: `DEADLINE_PASSED` or `SESSION_EXPIRED`), `SessionLeaseShortened`, `SessionClosed`, `Elected`, `Revoked`, `AcquireFailed`, `WorkCompleted` (the last four carry `kind`) |
| `ElectionKind` | `ELECTION`, `LOCK`, `GROUP`: which API started an election (on `Elected`, `Revoked` and `ElectionSnapshot`) |
| `WorkOutcome` | `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `SimbaSnapshot` | `session: SessionSnapshot`, `elections: List<ElectionSnapshot>`, `leaseDuration`, `healthy` |
| `SessionSnapshot` | `id`, `status` (`OPENING`, `LIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, `CLOSED`), `validFor`, `notLiveFor` |
| `ElectionSnapshot` | `name`, `status` (`CANDIDATE`, `LEADER`, `COOLDOWN`, `HANDOVER`), `token`, `remaining`, `kind` |

See [Observability](/guide/observability).

## Coroutines — `me.ahoo.simba.coroutines`

Module `simba-coroutines` (since 5.1).

| Type | Contract |
|---|---|
| `DistributedLock.awaitAcquire(timeout): LockTerm` | Suspending `acquireAsync`; cancellation abandons the attempt and releases a won term |
| `DistributedLock.awaitTryAcquire(): LockTerm?` | Suspending `tryAcquireAsync` |
| `DistributedLock.withLock(timeout, block: suspend (LockTerm) -> R): R` | Acquires, runs `block`, releases the term afterwards (also on failure or cancellation) |
| `Term.awaitRevoked(): RevokeReason` | Suspends until the term is revoked; cancelling the wait leaves the term alone |
| `SimbaEventFlow(bufferCapacity = 1024)` | `SimbaEventListener` whose `events: SharedFlow<SimbaEvent>` republishes events; drops the oldest for a slow collector |

See [Locks](/guide/locks#coroutines).

## Backend SPI — `me.ahoo.simba.spi`

```kotlin
interface LeaseBackend : AutoCloseable {
    val capabilities: Capabilities                    // releaseHints, membershipHints
    fun openSession(lease: Duration, metadata: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()): SessionGrant
    fun keepAlive(session: SessionId, lease: Duration, held: Set<LeaseName>): KeepAliveResult   // Live(remaining, owned) | Expired
    fun acquire(session: SessionId, names: Set<LeaseName>): Map<LeaseName, AcquireResult>      // Granted(token) | HeldBy(session, token)
    fun release(session: SessionId, leases: Map<LeaseName, Long>)
    fun closeSession(session: SessionId)
    fun join(session: SessionId, group: String)
    fun leave(session: SessionId, group: String)
    fun members(group: String): List<SessionId>
    fun subscribe(listener: BackendHintListener): AutoCloseable   // optional Released / MembersChanged hints
}
```

Rules every implementation follows (checked by [`LeaseBackendSpec`](/guide/testing#backend-tck)):

- every method makes a bounded number of backend calls, without waiting, scheduling, notifying or keeping local lease
  state;
- every remaining duration is computed with the backend's clock and returned as a duration, never a timestamp;
- a token is greater than zero, strictly increases with every new term of its name and never resets;
- a session expires once it was not kept alive for its lease, even if the transport keeps a connection alive;
- an expired session is never revived: `keepAlive` answers `Expired`, `acquire` throws `SessionExpiredException`;
- `keepAlive` reports every lease the session owns, whatever `held` says, and an owned lease lasts at least as long
  as its session, also on a backend whose leases expire on their own;
- inputs are validated alike, with `IllegalArgumentException`: leases of at least 1 ms, group names under the
  `LeaseName` rules, at most `LeaseBackend.MAX_BATCH` (64) names per `acquire`;
- `release` frees only leases the session still owns with exactly the given token, so a stale release is a no-op;
- hints only accelerate; losing one never affects correctness.

Value types: `LeaseName` (1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, not `.` or `..`), `SessionId` (never reused) —
both plain immutable classes with value equality, usable from Java — and `Ticker` (monotonic nanoseconds). Implementations: `JdbcLeaseBackend`, `RedisLeaseBackend`, `ZookeeperLeaseBackend`,
`InMemoryLeaseBackend`; see [Backends](/guide/backends).

## Spring Boot — `me.ahoo.simba.spring.boot.starter`

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `@SimbaScheduled(name, fixedDelay, fixedRate, initialDelay)` | Runs a method `()` or `(Term)` on `election(name).schedule(...)` |
| `@SimbaPartitioned(group, partitions, fixedDelay, fixedRate, initialDelay)` | Runs a method `(Term, Int)` on `group(group, partitions).schedule(...)` |
| `SimbaEndpoint` | Actuator endpoint `simba` |
| `SimbaHealthIndicator` | Health indicator `simba` |
| `MicrometerSimbaEventListener` | Micrometer meters from `SimbaEvent`s |

See [Spring Boot](/guide/configuration) and [Leader Work](/guide/leader-work#spring-annotations).
</doc>

<doc title="Architecture" path="architecture/index.md">
# Architecture

This page is for people changing Simba. It explains how the pieces fit and which rules they rely on;
[ADR 0010](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-simba-5-target-architecture.md) records why.

## Modules

```mermaid
graph BT
    core["simba-core<br>API, engine, SPI"]
    jdbc["simba-jdbc"]
    redis["simba-redis<br>Lua, RedisScripting"]
    sredis["simba-spring-redis<br>SpringRedisScripting"]
    zk["simba-zookeeper"]
    starter["simba-spring-boot-starter"]
    testing["simba-testing<br>in-memory backend, virtual time"]
    tck["simba-tck<br>LeaseBackendSpec, FencingSpec"]
    jdbc --> core
    redis --> core
    sredis --> redis
    zk --> core
    starter --> jdbc
    starter --> sredis
    starter --> zk
    testing --> core
    tck --> core
    style core fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style jdbc fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style redis fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style sredis fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style zk fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style starter fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style testing fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style tck fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

`simba-core` knows no backend and depends only on kotlin-logging. `simba-redis` must not depend on Spring; the
starter depends on the backends as optional features. `simba-bom` and `simba-dependencies` are publication metadata;
`simba-example` is a runnable sample per backend.

## Layers

| Layer | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| User API | `Simba`, `Election`, `DistributedLock`, `PartitionGroup`, `Term` | Handles; no state of their own beyond what the engine publishes |
| Engine | `engine.step(state, event, now)` | Pure state machine: no threads, clock or I/O |
| Shell | `EngineShell` | Runs `step` on one loop thread, executes its effects: backend calls, timers, callbacks, group views |
| SPI | `LeaseBackend` | A bounded number of calls per method: sessions, leases, groups, optional hints |

### The Pure Engine

```kotlin
fun step(state: EngineState, event: Event, now: Long): Pair<EngineState, List<Effect>>
```

Events are `Boot`, `Start`, `Stop`, `StepDown`, `Timer`, `Reply` (a backend result, tagged with its request id and send
time), `Hint`, `WorkExited`, `Join`, `Leave` and `Close`. Effects are `Call` (a backend request), `Arm` (a timer),
`Deadline` (publish the session's local deadline to its terms), `Elected` / `Revoked`, `Complete` (a future),
`Publish` (a `SimbaEvent`) and `Members` (a group view). Because `step` is pure, every race is a sequence of events: unit
tests feed events and assert effects, and the [simulation](/guide/testing#deterministic-simulation) explores
interleavings over thousands of seeds.

### The Election State Machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Candidate: start
    Candidate --> Leader: Granted(token), session live, before the deadline
    Candidate --> Candidate: HeldBy / retry after jitter or released hint
    Leader --> Candidate: deadline, TAKEN_OVER, SESSION_EXPIRED
    Leader --> Handover: stop / stepDown with work
    Handover --> Cooldown: work exited or deadline, release (stepDown)
    Handover --> [*]: work exited or deadline, release (stop)
    Leader --> Cooldown: stepDown without work
    Candidate --> Cooldown: stepDown
    Cooldown --> Candidate: cooldown over
    Leader --> [*]: stop without work
    Candidate --> [*]: stop
    Cooldown --> [*]: stop
```

Rules the engine keeps:

- A term is adopted only from the reply to the election's current attempt, before the session's local deadline, and
  only with a token above every token the session released for that name.
- A term is revoked before its lease is released; releases carry the token.
- Keep-alive replies list the leases the session owns: a term adopted before the request but missing from the reply is
  revoked (`TAKEN_OVER`); an owned lease that nobody holds or is acquiring is released.
- An expired session is never revived: every term is revoked and a new session is opened.
- Handover: an election started with work keeps the lease of a stopped or stepped-down term until the work exited or
  the session's local deadline at the stop, whichever comes first; terms without work release at once.

## Threads

| Thread | Runs |
|---|---|
| Loop (one platform thread per client) | `step`, timers; the only thread touching engine state |
| I/O executor (default: a virtual thread per call) | Backend calls, with a timeout of one renew interval; at most one keep-alive per session and one acquire per election in flight |
| Callback executor (default: virtual threads) | `onElected` / `onRevoked`, through one serial dispatcher per election |
| Work executor (default: a virtual thread per term) | `runWhileLeader` / `schedule` / group work; interrupted on revocation |

The engine never waits for a callback except through the futures of `stop()` and `stepDown()`. Blocking `close()`
methods do not wait when called from a callback or leader work. `SimbaEventListener`s are called from the loop.

## Time

- The client never reads a wall clock for lease decisions. Every remaining time comes from the backend as a duration,
  and the local deadline is `sentAt + remaining × (1 − drift) − margin` on the monotonic clock (`Ticker`).
- `Term.isValid` and `remaining()` read the session's volatile deadline and the ticker; no watchdog thread has to run.
- Backends decide with their own clock: database `now` (JDBC), Redis `TIME`, Zookeeper session expiry.

## Wire Contracts

Nodes of the same major version may run together, so these must not change within 5.x:

- **Lease names:** 1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; partition `p` of group `g` is `{g}.{p}`.
- **Partition assignment:** `PartitionAssignment.weight` (FNV-1a 64 of `"$partition@$member"` mixed with SplitMix64,
  members are session ids).
- **JDBC:** tables `simba_session`, `simba_lease`, `simba_member`; `simba_lease` rows are never deleted and release
  clears `session_id` only; every time comparison uses the dialect's `now` (UTC epoch ms); the take-over reads the
  holder's session row `for share`, serializing with its keep-alive; the MySQL acquire assigns `token` before
  `session_id` (left-to-right `SET`).
- **Redis:** `simba:lease:{name}` = `{session, token, expires}` (never expires, never deleted),
  `simba:session:{sid}` (`PX`) with `:leases` / `:groups`, `simba:group:{g}` scored by expiry, `released` published on
  the lease key; with `routeBySlot` every script call stays within one hash slot.
- **Zookeeper:** ephemeral `/simba/leases/{name}` (token = `czxid`), `/simba/groups/{g}/{sid}`.

## Design Records

| ADR | Decision |
|---|---|
| [0010](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-simba-5-target-architecture.md) | Simba 5: sessions, terms, a pure engine, one `LeaseBackend` SPI (supersedes 0001–0009 where they conflict) |
| [0002](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-fencing-token.md) | Fencing tokens; still holds |
| [0001](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-lease-contention-engine.md), [0003](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-simba-4.md)–[0009](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-partitioned-leadership.md) | The 4.x design: lease engine, 4.0, leader scheduling, observability, Actuator endpoint, lease validity and health, relinquish and handover, partitioned leadership |
</doc>

<doc title="Contributing" path="contributing/index.md">
# Contributing

The workflow, commit conventions, quality gates and release process are defined in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). This page covers the technical side.
Read [Architecture](/architecture/) first; the invariants an agent or reviewer checks are listed in
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Simba/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

## Build and Test

You need JDK 21 and Docker.

```bash
./gradlew build                                   # all modules
./gradlew simba-core:check                        # tests + detekt for one module
./gradlew simba-core:test --tests me.ahoo.simba.engine.EngineTest
./gradlew simba-testing:test -Psimba.simulation.seed=42   # replay one simulation seed
./gradlew simba-example:check -PexampleBackend=jdbc   # jdbc | redis | zookeeper (default: redis)
./gradlew codeCoverageReport                      # aggregated JaCoCo report
./gradlew test -PtestJavaVersion=25               # run tests on another JDK; bytecode stays 21
```

| Module | Test infrastructure |
|---|---|
| `simba-core`, `simba-testing`, `simba-tck` | None |
| `simba-zookeeper` | Embedded Curator `TestingServer` |
| `simba-redis` (also covers `simba-spring-redis`) | Testcontainers `redis:7.4-alpine` (`RedisFixture`) |
| `simba-jdbc` | Testcontainers `mysql:8.4` and `postgres:17` (`LeaseDatabaseFixture`) |
| `simba-spring-boot-starter` | Spring Boot test slices |

## Writing Tests

- Name tests after the behavior. Assertions use FluentAssert (`.assert()`); MockK only when a real code path is
  impractical.
- Never `sleep` to synchronize; wait on queues, latches or futures.
- **Engine changes** are tested as tables of events in and effects out against `step()`, with no executor. Keep
  `SimulationSpec` (the invariants over 10⁴ seeds) green.
- **Threaded client tests** run on virtual time: `VirtualScheduler`, direct I/O and callback executors, and
  `awaitIdle()` between timers (see `VirtualSimba` in the `simba-testing` tests).
- Backend semantics are tested once, in the TCK.

## Adding a Backend

1. Implement `LeaseBackend`: a bounded number of calls per method, no scheduling, no local lease state, remaining
   times measured by the backend's clock and returned as durations, tokens that strictly increase and never reset,
   expired sessions that are never revived, keep-alive replies that list every owned lease.
2. Extend [`LeaseBackendSpec`](/guide/testing#backend-tck) for it. A backend with an injectable clock overrides
   `clock`; otherwise time-based tests poll until the backend's own lease ran out.
3. Add a starter auto-configuration activated by `simba.enabled`, `simba.<backend>.enabled` and `simba.backend`,
   registered in `META-INF/spring/...AutoConfiguration.imports` and `additional-spring-configuration-metadata.json`,
   plus a `SimbaBackend` entry and an example backend.
4. Document it in [Backends](/guide/backends) (both languages).

Open an issue first: a new backend, dependency, change of the `LeaseBackend` SPI, the Redis scripts or key names,
the JDBC SQL or schema, or the public `simba-core` API needs agreement before code.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `README.md` / `README.zh-CN.md` | Landing page: what Simba is, install, one example per API |

| `docs/adr/` | Design decisions and their rationale |
| `AGENTS.md` | Invariants and traps for maintainers and coding agents |

Every page change is made in both languages. After editing English pages, regenerate `wiki/llms-full.txt`:

```bash
cd wiki
pnpm install
pnpm run sync:llms
pnpm run build
```
</doc>
